scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a paginated and filtered list of all customer point wallets as an admin. The test should include standard listing, using various filters such as specific customer associations and balance ranges, and sorting the results. Ensure only admins can access this endpoint. Edge cases include: using invalid filter formats, attempting access with a non-admin role, and validating that only expected records are returned as per filters. Verify audit log is generated for the query according to compliance.

Test error response when a non-admin user attempts to retrieve the paginated point wallet list. The scenario should confirm that access is denied and an appropriate error code is returned for compliance logging.

Test successful retrieval of categories with search filters and pagination. Set up at least one parent category and one child to validate hierarchy in the response. The request should include a filter on code or name, as well as paging parameters (e.g., page, size), and optionally test visibility/status filtering. Ensure the response includes both top-level and nested categories, only those not soft-deleted, and that paging/sorting work as expected. Permission errors and malformed request errors should be included as negative scenarios. Attempt this as an admin user, as required.

dependencies.purpose: Ensure the existence of an admin account to obtain a valid admin JWT for authorization.
Create at least one parent and one child category as test data for filtering, hierarchy, and pagination tests.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieval of a specific category by UUID as an admin. First, create a new category and use its ID to request details; ensure all returned fields match what was created, including hierarchy and status flags. Next, request with a non-existent or soft-deleted categoryId and expect a not found error. Also, check the response to permission errors if the role is not admin.

dependencies.purpose: Ensure admin provider exists and obtain JWT for authenticated calls.
Create a new category to obtain a valid UUID for detail retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Test creating a new category as an admin. Provide valid input including unique code, name, and optionally parent_id. On success, confirm all fields are persisted and valid. Attempt to create a category with a duplicate code (should fail with appropriate error). Attempt to create with an invalid or non-existent parent_id and check for error response. Also, attempt as a non-admin and verify permission denial.

dependencies.purpose: Create and login an admin user for valid authorized creation.
Create an initial category to use its code for duplicate and its ID for valid/invalid parent_id tests.

scenarios.draft: Test updating an existing category (name, parent, display order, etc.) as an admin. First, create a category, then update its name and verify the change persists. Attempt to update with a duplicate code (should error). Try to update with a non-existent or deleted categoryId and expect not found. Attempt update as a non-admin and ensure permission denied. Also, test reparenting to an invalid parent and for integrity on parent/child relationships.

dependencies.purpose: Ensure admin test user exists for authorization.
Create two categories to test update, duplicate code, and reparenting scenarios.

scenarios.draft: Test soft-deleting an existing category by its UUID as an admin. First, create a category and then delete it, verifying that the deleted_at field is set and it's excluded from subsequent searches. Attempt to delete a non-existent or already-deleted category and verify the system returns an appropriate error. Also, create a category with an active child and try to delete the parent; expect either an error or forced cascade behavior as per admin UI logic. Permission enforcement should be validated by attempting this operation as a non-admin as well.

dependencies.purpose: Have a valid admin account for performing deletes.
Create one or more categories (with parent/child relation if necessary) to be soft deleted.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieval of a specific product-category mapping detail by a seller for a product the seller owns. Ensure that the call succeeds and returns all relevant mapping and category data. Verify edge case: if the mapping does not belong to the seller or does not exist, the API responds with an access denied or not found error. Also test that an admin can view any mapping, but a seller can only view their own product's mapping. Attempt access as a different seller to ensure proper permission enforcement.

dependencies.purpose: Create a product as a seller to establish ownership for the product-category mapping. Required prior to creating the mapping.
Create a product-category mapping to obtain a valid productCategoryMapId for the detail-fetching scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin can successfully retrieve the details of any product-category mapping by specifying productId and productCategoryMapId. Confirm that returned data includes all relational context and business fields. Test error conditions: request with a non-existent mapping, request with a mapping for a soft-deleted product, and request as a non-admin for an access denied error. Ensure audit logging is triggered on access for compliance.

dependencies.purpose: Create a product to supply a valid productId for category mapping.
Create a product-category mapping as an admin to obtain a productCategoryMapId for testing detail retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Test creating a new product-category mapping for a seller's product. Confirm success when mapping a valid product with a new category, and that all fields are validated. Set up: product and category must exist, and the user must be the owning seller. Also test creating a mapping with duplicate category or illegal parent-child links, expecting a validation or conflict error. Handle edge cases: non-existent product/category, forbidden access if not product owner, and soft-deleted product.

dependencies.purpose: Create a product as a seller to use as the source for the mapping.
Create a category to be mapped to the product.

scenarios.draft: Test an admin creating a product-category mapping for any product and category. Ensure mapping is created if all references are valid and no duplicate mapping exists. Expect validation errors if trying to map to a soft-deleted or non-existent product or category. Try to create a duplicate mapping and expect a conflict error. Ensure audit logging occurs for compliance.

dependencies.purpose: Provision a product for mapping via the admin role.
Provision a category for mapping to the product.

scenarios.draft: Test updating an existing product-category mapping for a product owned by the seller. Confirm allowed fields (such as the 'primary' flag or audit notes) can be updated successfully. Attempt updates with invalid or out-of-scope fields to provoke a validation error. Check error cases: updating a non-existent or unauthorized mapping returns access denied or not found. Ensure audit log entries are created for each update as per business rules. Attempt to update as a different seller to ensure permissions are enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Create a product as a seller before managing mappings.
Create an initial product-category mapping to test updates on.

scenarios.draft: Test searching and paginating channel-category mappings as an admin with various filters applied. Prepare existing channels and categories, then create mappings with different channel/category pairings and statuses. Use this endpoint to retrieve mappings filtered by channel, category, active/deleted status, and time windows, verifying that results only include records matching the filter, are properly paginated, and include expected relational metadata. Success requires that only authorized admin users receive results and that audit logging for the search occurs.

dependencies.purpose: Create a business channel to be mapped to categories.
Create a category to be mapped to channels.
Create a mapping between a channel and a category to ensure records exist for search and filter.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a specific channel-category mapping by its UUID as an admin. First, create a channel, a category, and a mapping joining them. Retrieve the mapping by its ID and verify that all business and relational fields are present. Also test error cases by attempting to retrieve a non-existent or soft-deleted mapping, expecting a 'not found' error and appropriate audit logging.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new admin business channel for mapping.
Create a new category for mapping.
Create the mapping entity to obtain its UUID for retrieval testing.

scenarios.draft: Test creating a new mapping between an existing admin channel and category. First, create a channel and a category as admin. Attempt mapping creation with valid channel and category, and expect success. Then, try to create the same mapping again to test duplicate constraint and expect a business validation error. Also test mapping creation with non-existent or soft-deleted channel/category references and verify that the API responds with 'not found' or 'invalid reference' errors, and proper audit logging occurs for all actions.

dependencies.purpose: Create a business channel for mapping.
Create a category for mapping.

scenarios.draft: Test updating an existing channel-category mapping record as admin. First, ensure existence by creating channel, category, and mapping. Update the mapping's business fields such as changing the category or updating status (if applicable) and verify success. Also, attempt to change mapping to a (channel, category) combination that would create a duplicate and expect an error. Test updating with invalid or non-existent mapping UUID and verify that API responds with suitable errors. All changes must be audit-logged.

dependencies.purpose: Create a business channel for mapping.
Create a category for mapping.
Create the mapping entity to be updated.

scenarios.draft: Test deleting (soft-delete) a channel-category mapping by its UUID as admin. First, create the necessary channel, category, and mapping. Perform a delete and verify that mapping is excluded from active queries but preserved for audit. Attempt to delete an already-deleted or non-existent mapping and expect a 'not found' or idempotency error. Finally, confirm that unauthorized actors cannot execute this operation and that all events are logged in the audit trail.

dependencies.purpose: Create a business channel for mapping.
Create a category for mapping.
Create the mapping entity to be deleted.

scenarios.draft: Test admin panel's customer search endpoint with advanced filters and pagination. The admin must be authenticated to access results. Verify responses for matched customers with privacy-masked data, test filtering by email, nickname, dates, phone verify status, and paging controls. Confirm full response shape, and confirm error handling for malformed filters or unauthorized access. Test that soft-deleted users do not appear.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as admin to gain access token for customer search.

scenarios.draft: Verify that an admin can retrieve the full profile for any customer by valid customerId, including sensitive fields (email, status, etc), and that requesting a non-existent or soft-deleted customer returns a not found error. Confirm permission errors if using a token not tied to admin or improper role. Confirm field-level security for edge cases.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as admin for authorization.
Register a new customer account to ensure a valid customerId exists.

scenarios.draft: Confirm that a customer can successfully retrieve their own profile with full detail by specifying their customerId, but that attempts to access another customer's profile are forbidden. Ensure sensitive audit and profile fields are included for self, and masked or restricted for others. Validate behavior for non-existent and soft-deleted targets.

dependencies.purpose: Register new customers to provide customerId context for self and other-access tests.
Login as one customer to retrieve their own token for proper access control.

scenarios.draft: Check that an admin can successfully update a customer's profile fields (name, email, phone, etc.) if the fields pass all validations. Test that business rules are enforced—such as unique email and valid phone format. Confirm full audit logging occurs. Also test trying to update a customer to an already-used email or with invalid phone—expect corresponding validation errors. Attempt to update a non-existent or soft-deleted user results in a not found error.

dependencies.purpose: Login as admin to get authorization for update action.
Register multiple customer accounts for update and uniqueness conflict testing.

scenarios.draft: Ensure a customer can update their own profile fields when providing valid new data (such as name, phone, etc.), and the changes are reflected in their profile. Attempt updates with invalid or already used email, or invalid phone format to validate client-side and server-side errors are returned. Check that trying to update another customer's profile or a soft-deleted account is forbidden or fails with appropriate errors.

dependencies.purpose: Register two or more customer accounts for conflict and permission validation.
Login as one customer to receive a proper auth token for update attempts.

scenarios.draft: Test searching and paginating an admin user's audit history with filter, pagination, and sort options. Set up an admin account, perform a number of actions to generate audit events (such as login/logout and updates), then query their history specifying a filter (e.g., action type or date range) and a page size. Verify the response contains the correct number of history records, applies filters, and returns pagination metadata. Also ensure search does not leak sensitive data to unauthorized requestors.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin account for which to collect audit history.
Log in as admin to generate audit events for the admin user.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a specific admin history record by adminId and historyId, covering both success and error cases. First, register an admin and perform actions to ensure history is generated. Obtain an existing history record's ID and fetch its detail, verifying all expected metadata and before/after state. Then test access with an invalid or non-existent ID, and attempt access as an unauthorized user to confirm error and permission handling.

dependencies.purpose: Create admin for whom history records will be generated.
Log in as admin to perform actions and produce history records.
Search and list history records to obtain valid historyId for detail fetch.

scenarios.draft: Test advanced product search by admin with various combinations of filters (such as category, seller, status, and name) and pagination parameters. Ensure that search returns only products matching the criteria, respects page size and ordering, and does not leak data across unauthorized roles. Include queries for both empty results (no product matches) and active products. Cover edge cases such as invalid filters and excessively large page requests.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an admin, required to access product search API.
Log in as admin to perform product search requests.

scenarios.draft: Test that a seller can search for their own products using filter, pagination, and sort criteria, and verify that products outside of their scope are not included. Create test sellers, products owned by each seller, and confirm that the search returns only the authenticated seller's products. Include at least one case where the result set is empty due to filtering. Also test unauthorized access or attempting to use admin-only filters as a seller.

dependencies.purpose: Register one or more seller accounts to test search result scoping.
Authenticate as a seller to perform product search and confirm RBAC scoping.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin can retrieve detailed information for a specific product by productId. Cover both successful retrieval (all attributes, links to categories or seller) and error scenarios (non-existent productId, product is soft-deleted, or access as non-admin). Also verify that sensitive fields are present or masked correctly based on admin authorization, and that attempted access to deleted or unauthorized records triggers appropriate errors.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate as an admin for making detail fetch requests.
Log in as admin to authorize product detail retrieval.
Create products as admin to ensure there are records for detail retrieval and not-found tests.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieval of a specific seller history record by admin. Scenario covers: 1) Successful fetch for an existing seller and historyId with all details (e.g., after a seller status update or compliance event); 2) Attempt to fetch a history record that does not exist (expect not found error); 3) Access control check—only admin users should succeed, other roles should be denied; 4) Attempt to access a history record not belonging to the given sellerId (expect not found or forbidden). Precondition: A seller with recorded action history must exist.

dependencies.purpose: Log in as admin to acquire a valid JWT for authorized access.
Search and select an existing seller with sufficient action history.
Obtain a list of actual seller history records to locate a valid historyId for positive and negative tests.

scenarios.draft: Test admin user search and paginated retrieval. Scenarios: 1) Retrieve the first page of admin accounts with default filters—confirm pagination metadata, summary fields present; 2) Use filter criteria such as role or status to restrict the result set; 3) Apply a date range filter to restrict admins by creation or modification date; 4) Submit a query with no matching results (expect empty dataset, valid pagination response); 5) Attempt to use the endpoint as a non-admin user—verify access is denied with appropriate error.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as admin to perform admin-level actions and searches.

scenarios.draft: Test fetching detailed information for a specific admin account by adminId. Scenarios: 1) Successfully fetch details for a valid admin—check that sensitive fields (like password hash) are excluded, but all profile/role details are present; 2) Attempt with a non-existent adminId—expect not found error; 3) Attempt with insufficient permissions (non-admin JWT)—expect forbidden or unauthorized error.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as admin to perform authorized lookup.
Get or search for existing admin IDs for use in positive and negative test scenarios.

scenarios.draft: Test update of an admin account's non-password fields as an admin. Scenarios: 1) Successfully update permissible fields of an existing admin (role/status/profile info), verify update is reflected in subsequent GET; 2) Attempt update with missing or invalid fields—expect validation error; 3) Attempt update with an ID that does not exist—expect not found error; 4) Ensure password changes are blocked by this endpoint and only allowed through the dedicated password flow; 5) Attempt update with a non-admin (unauthorized) role—expect forbidden error.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an admin to obtain privileges for update.
Obtain a list of active admins with updatable fields.

scenarios.draft: Test soft-deletion of admin accounts (set deleted_at). Scenarios: 1) Successfully delete an active admin account and confirm it is excluded from subsequent searches; 2) Repeat delete against the same adminId (already soft-deleted)—expect not found or idempotent result; 3) Attempt to delete a non-existent adminId—expect proper error; 4) Attempt deletion with insufficient permissions (non-admin JWT)—expect forbidden/unauthorized; 5) Confirm audit/history record is generated for the deletion event.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as admin for delete privileges.
List available admin accounts for deletion test.

scenarios.draft: Test basic log search functionality for a specific attachment, including pagination, event_type filtering (e.g., upload, download), and date range. Validate that only log entries related to the specified attachmentId are returned, that pagination metadata is correct, and that results exclude soft-deleted records. Attempt filter combinations for edge cases such as empty result sets or overly broad filters. Ensure error scenarios for invalid attachmentId or malformed filters. Only accessible by admins. Dependencies: creation of a file attachment and multiple log entries for that attachment.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new attachment file to obtain a valid attachmentId and test various log event searches on it.
Create several different types of log entries (e.g., upload, download, access) for the attachment to test search variation and filter accuracy.

scenarios.draft: Test fetching a single attachment log entry by attachmentId and attachmentLogId as an admin. Scenario must confirm success when correct IDs are supplied, including all expected audit fields (event_type, operated_by_admin_id, event_context, event_at, etc.), and appropriate error responses (404 or permission denied) in cases where the log does not exist, the attachment has been deleted, or the log ID is not linked to the attachment. Also test with unauthorized role to verify enforcement of admin-only access. Dependencies: register a file attachment, create log entry, and (for negative testing) erase the log and test post-delete attempts.

dependencies.purpose: Create a test attachment to have a real attachmentId for log record creation.
Add a log entry to the created attachment, producing a valid attachmentLogId for retrieval tests.

scenarios.draft: Test creation of a new attachment log record by supplying all required log details (event_type, event_at, ip_address, operated_by_admin_id). Ensure the new log is persisted, appears in subsequent log searches for the attachment, and that all fields match the request or expected system-generated values. Test with missing/invalid event_type, invalid attachmentId, or missing required parameters to confirm proper validation and error responses. Attempt to create logs for non-existent or already deleted attachments and confirm error handling. Only admins may create logs. Dependencies: create an attachment to provide a valid attachmentId, and erase the attachment for negative path testing.

dependencies.purpose: Create an attachment file to test log creation for a valid attachmentId.

scenarios.draft: Test updating mutable metadata fields (such as event_context or operated_by_admin_id if permitted) in a specific attachment log record. Verify that updates succeed only when provided fields are allowed for mutation by the schema, and that immutable fields like event_type, event_at, and ip_address cannot be changed (attempt to update them should yield a validation error). Check audit trail compliance, and attempt updates with invalid or non-existent log/attachment IDs. Dependencies: create a test attachment and log entry to update.

dependencies.purpose: Create an attachment entity to allow subsequent log operations.
Add a log entry to the test attachment, obtaining both attachmentId and attachmentLogId for update operations.

scenarios.draft: Test deletion of an attachment log entry by attachmentId and attachmentLogId as an admin. Verify that after deletion, the log entry cannot be retrieved by GET. Check compliance logging for the delete operation. Attempt to delete an already-deleted, non-existent, or unrelated (wrong attachment) log and expect proper error codes. Only admins can delete attachment logs via this endpoint. Dependencies: create an attachment, create a log entry, and verify log existence before and after the delete operation.

dependencies.purpose: Register an attachment for log manipulation.
Create a log entry to later target for deletion and validation.

scenarios.draft: Test the admin's ability to successfully retrieve a paginated and filtered list of shopping cart records. Set up at least one customer and shopping cart in the system with various statuses and customers. As an authenticated admin, request a filtered list (e.g., filter by status or customer info) and verify that the response is correctly paginated, contains the expected carts, and includes all relevant metadata according to the schema. Confirm only permitted carts are visible and the summary fields match the database.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as admin to obtain an access token for subsequent authorized API calls.
Create sample customer cart records to ensure there is data to paginate/filter in the admin search.

scenarios.draft: Test that the admin search endpoint handles invalid or malformed search criteria gracefully (e.g., passing a non-allowed field or wrong data type as a filter). As an admin, send an unrecognized field or an invalid value type in the request. The service should return a validation error with an appropriate code and description, and error logs should capture the bad request for audit.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as admin for permission to use the admin cart search endpoint.

scenarios.draft: Test that a customer can retrieve the full details of their own cart by cartId. Register and login as a customer, create a cart, and then fetch its detail using the returned cartId. Validate that all fields in the response match the cart record and business data for the correct customer. Check that unauthorized access to a cart not owned by the user is denied with an appropriate error message.

dependencies.purpose: Register and log in as a customer to obtain an access token.
Create a new cart as the customer, from which you will retrieve the cartId for detail access.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin is able to retrieve the full details of any cart by cartId. As an authenticated admin, create at least one cart through customer functionality and then, using its cartId, retrieve the detail through the admin endpoint. Validate that all metadata (status, customer, session, audit fields) are correct and visible. Attempting to access a cart with an invalid or non-existent cartId must yield a 'not found' or validation error.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as admin for admin-level access.
Create a cart as a customer to ensure a record exists for admin retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Test creation of a new shopping cart by an authenticated customer. Register and log in as a new customer, then create a fresh cart specifying initial status and customer linkage. Verify the returned cart record contains all required schema fields, the status is correct, and only one active cart per customer is allowed per policy. Attempt to create a second active cart as the same customer and verify that the system blocks the duplicate and returns a descriptive business rule error.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate a customer who will create the cart.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin can create a shopping cart on behalf of a valid customer. Authenticate as admin, ensure the target customer exists, and create a cart via the admin POST endpoint providing customerId and initial status. The returned cart must be linked to the specified customer and comply with business policies like preventing multiple active carts. Attempt creation with an invalid or non-existent customerId and confirm the service returns a validation or not-found error.

dependencies.purpose: Login as admin for API authorization.
Register a customer to serve as the owner of the admin-created cart.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a paginated and filtered list of order snapshot records for a specific order as a customer. Scenario includes creating a new order, performing multiple order status changes (e.g., payment, shipment), and then retrieving the snapshot list to verify that all key state changes have been captured. The test verifies pagination works, filtering by date or reason is respected, and only the owning customer has access. Error tests: invalid or unauthorized orderId, misconfigured pagination, or insufficient permissions.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new order as a customer to ensure snapshot data exists and customer context is valid.
Change order status multiple times to trigger new snapshots being created.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving the full detail of a specific order snapshot for an order as an admin. Steps include creating an order as a customer, creating an order snapshot (e.g., after status update or payment), then using the admin endpoint to fetch a specific snapshot by orderId and orderSnapshotId. This validates that all archived fields are present and accurate for audit/compliance purposes. Also, test error scenarios for requesting nonexistent orderSnapshotIds or orders, and attempt access with insufficient permissions.

dependencies.purpose: Create the order and ensure a valid business context for an order snapshot.
Create an order snapshot for the order so that orderSnapshotId can be obtained and used for retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Test that a seller can retrieve a detailed order snapshot for an order associated with their products. First, create a seller and associated product, have a customer place an order for that product, confirm the order belongs to the seller, create an order snapshot via status history change or admin action, and then verify the seller can fetch the snapshot detail. Test negative cases for a seller requesting a snapshot for an order they do not own or for a deleted/nonexistent snapshot.

dependencies.purpose: Create a product associated with the seller.
Simulate customer placing order for the seller's product.
Create a valid order snapshot for this flow.

scenarios.draft: Test that a customer can retrieve the archived details of their own order's specific snapshot. Workflow: create customer and order, perform status changes to create at least one snapshot, and ensure that the customer can access the snapshot detail by correct combination of orderId and orderSnapshotId. Validate that all expected details are returned. Test error cases where the snapshot does not exist, the order is not owned by the customer, or the snapshot was deleted or access is forbidden.

dependencies.purpose: Create an order as a customer to generate snapshot data.
Generate a snapshot event for the test order.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin can create a new order snapshot for a particular order, used for compliance or forensic record keeping. Flow: customer places and pays for an order, and admin performs snapshot creation at a key business event (e.g., before fulfillment or after payment). Validate snapshot content matches current order state and is immutable after creation. Include negative scenarios for attempts on orders not found, already deleted, or insufficient admin privileges.

dependencies.purpose: Create a real order with valid business context for snapshot operation.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieval of a specific tag associated with a seller's product. Scenario includes: (1) successfully fetching tag detail as the owning seller; (2) attempting to fetch a non-existent tag (expect not found error); (3) trying to access a tag on a product not owned by the seller (expect forbidden error); (4) handling of access after the tag has been deleted. Prerequisites include creation of a seller, product, and tag, and (for unauthorized cases) creating a second seller or using a non-owner context.

dependencies.purpose: Register the seller account that will own the product and tag.
Log in as the seller to acquire authentication token for authorization.
Create a product under the seller to attach a tag.
Create a tag on the product to retrieve its detail.

scenarios.draft: Test admin access to the detail of a product tag. Covers: (1) admin successfully retrieves any product tag detail (even for products not owned by the admin); (2) attempt by admin to fetch a non-existent product tag (should return not found error). Previous creation of at least one admin account and a product tag by a seller is needed. Also test error handling when tag is already deleted.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate an admin account for authorization.
Log in as admin to acquire access token.
Register a seller, as only sellers can create products and tags.
Authenticate as seller to create a product and product tag.
Seller creates a product to which the tag will be attached.
Seller creates a tag to be later accessed by admin.

scenarios.draft: Test successful creation of a product tag by the owning seller, including required validations (unique tag per product, valid tag string). Also test error on duplicate tag (same tag string for the same product, should fail), and error for missing/invalid fields. Covers scenario when a seller tries to create a tag on a product they do not own (expect forbidden).

dependencies.purpose: Register the seller account for authentication.
Obtain authentication token as seller.
Create a product to which to add tags.

scenarios.draft: Test creating a product tag as an admin on any product. Covers (1) successful tag creation (providing all fields per business logic), (2) creating a tag with invalid or duplicate data (same tag string—should fail), (3) assigning a tag to a non-existent product (expect not found). Assures that admins can create tags on products regardless of original owner.

dependencies.purpose: Create admin account for authentication.
Admin login for authorization.
Create a seller to later create a product.
Log in as seller to create a product as the basis for admin tag creation.
Create a product under the seller for testing admin tag creation.

scenarios.draft: Test updating a product tag as the owning seller. Scenarios: (1) successfully update tag details (such as tag string/title), (2) attempt to update with an invalid or duplicate tag string (should fail validation), (3) try to update a tag on a product not owned by the seller (expect forbidden), and (4) update a tag that no longer exists (expect not found). Requires previous setup of seller, authentication, product, and tag. Also, negative test for non-existent tag and non-existent product IDs.

dependencies.purpose: Register the seller account for product and tag management.
Authenticate seller for authorization.
Create product to attach tags to.
Create a product tag for update scenarios.

scenarios.draft: Test successful customer login with valid email and password when the account is active and email verified. Ensure JWT is issued and last_login_at and audit events are updated accordingly. This scenario requires a prior customer registration with a unique email and password, followed by an update to set the status as active and email_verified as true.

dependencies.purpose: Register a customer with a unique email to prepare for login scenario.
Update customer status to 'active' and set 'email_verified' to true for login eligibility.

scenarios.draft: Test login failure scenario with a valid email but incorrect password. Confirm the system returns the appropriate error for authentication failure and logs the attempt without issuing a JWT.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new customer for testing login failures.

scenarios.draft: Test login when the customer account is locked. Attempt authentication with valid credentials and verify the response denies access, provides a clear error, and does not issue a JWT.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new customer for testing.
Set customer's status to 'locked' to test access denial during login.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to log in with valid credentials when the email_verified field is false. System should deny login and provide a clear error message that email verification is required.

dependencies.purpose: Register a customer and ensure email_verified remains false before attempting login.

scenarios.draft: Test successful logout for an authenticated customer by invalidating the JWT token. Ensure the audit log in customer_histories is updated and subsequent requests with the same token are rejected.

dependencies.purpose: Register and obtain a JWT for a new customer.
Login to acquire valid JWT for session.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to logout without a valid JWT (unauthenticated request) and ensure an error is returned indicating no active session or unauthenticated state.

Validate a JWT token for a logged-in customer. Ensure the endpoint affirms the token is valid, returns customer details, and the session remains active. JWT must be acquired through prior successful login.

dependencies.purpose: Register and obtain valid credentials for a customer.
Login to receive valid JWT for validation.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to validate an expired, tampered with, or otherwise invalid JWT. The system should respond with an error, invalidating the session and not returning any customer details.

Test successful password change for an authenticated customer by providing the correct current password and a new strong password that meets policy requirements. JWT session should be reset, and customer_histories should record the change.

dependencies.purpose: Register and login as customer to receive authentication.
Obtain JWT to authorize password change request.

scenarios.draft: Attempt password change with an incorrect current password. Ensure the operation fails, the password is not updated, and error detail is returned without session interruption.

dependencies.purpose: Register and login as customer for valid JWT.

scenarios.draft: Attempt password change operation with no or invalid authentication (JWT), and verify that the system returns a permission error and does not update the password.

Register a new admin with a unique email and valid password. Ensure JWT is issued, admin record is stored, and required audit logs are recorded. The response must include setHeaders with Authorization for JWT usage.
Attempt to register an admin using an email address that already exists in the system. The operation should fail with a unique constraint error and no account or JWT is created.

dependencies.purpose: Register the initial admin for email duplication test.

scenarios.draft: Test successful deletion of a business verification record by a seller. Register a new seller, complete authentication, and create a required business verification record (such as uploading valid business documents). Then, as the seller, delete the created business verification using the given sellerId and businessVerificationId. Ensure the record is removed and an audit entry is created. Confirm that attempts to retrieve the deleted record return not found or compliance error.

dependencies.purpose: Register and onboard a new seller in order to have a valid authenticated account.
Authenticate seller to retrieve the necessary JWT token for authorized business verification operations.
Create a business verification record (such as business license or other documents) attached to sellerId.

scenarios.draft: Test successful deletion of a seller business verification record by an admin. First, onboard a seller and ensure a business verification record exists. Then, login as an admin and delete the business verification record using the provided sellerId and businessVerificationId. Validate response and ensure that the record cannot be retrieved afterwards by any role. Confirm proper audit trail logging per compliance.

dependencies.purpose: Register and onboard an admin account for performing administrative actions.
Authenticate as admin to acquire authorization for the operation.
Create a seller for the business verification record.
Seller authenticates to create one or more business verification records.
Create a business verification record from the seller account in order to have an existing record to delete.

scenarios.draft: Test searching and retrieving seller onboarding history via the seller endpoint. Register a new seller, log in to obtain a token, and then initiate onboarding events (such as document uploads, AI reviews, or step progressions). Use PATCH to query onboarding event records for the sellerId and validate correct filtering, ordering, and pagination. Ensure only onboarding events related to the authenticated seller are returned and data privacy is maintained.

dependencies.purpose: Onboard a seller account to access onboarding history endpoints.
Authenticate as seller for authorized operations.
Add at least one onboarding event to enable meaningful search results.

scenarios.draft: Test admin search and filter of onboarding events for a specific sellerId. Register both an admin and a seller. Ensure onboarding history exists. Use PATCH API as admin to query onboarding events and validate results include all appropriate onboarding records for that seller, supporting filter/pagination, and verify unauthorized access is blocked for non-admins. Cross-verify audit trails for compliance.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin for making admin API calls.
Authenticate as admin for authorization.
Create a seller and obtain sellerId.
Have seller onboarding history created so that admin search yields meaningful data.

scenarios.draft: Test fetching the details of a specific onboarding event by the seller, given a valid sellerId and onboardingId. Register and authenticate a seller, create at least one onboarding record, and then retrieve the onboarding event using GET. Validate the full onboarding details match expected values and that unauthorized access (e.g., by another seller) is properly denied. Include error scenarios for invalid or non-existent onboardingId.

dependencies.purpose: Create seller account and retrieve sellerId.
Authenticate as the target seller.
Create a specific onboarding event to be queried in detail.

scenarios.draft: Test searching for attachments with various filters as an admin. Scenario includes applying filters such as file_name, mime_type, owner_type, and size, as well as testing pagination. Verify only users with admin roles can access full results, and results exclude expired or unauthorized files. Edge cases: request with no filters (returns all permitted), invalid filter input (returns descriptive error), and request with filters that return empty result sets. Validate audit log entry is created each time.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin to perform authorized searches.
Create multiple attachments as test data for filter and pagination validations.

scenarios.draft: Test successful retrieval of full attachment metadata by UUID as an admin. Verify all required metadata fields are returned, including storage URI, mime type, hash, and all attachment business context fields. Attempt access as unauthorized role or for non-existent attachmentId to validate error handling and access restrictions. Edge case: trying to fetch a soft deleted (expire/retired) file as an admin (should succeed), and regular user (should be denied).

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin for authorization.
Create an attachment whose ID will be used to fetch details.

scenarios.draft: Test creating a new attachment with all required metadata fields (owner_id, owner_type, file_name, file_size, mime_type, storage_uri, hash_sha256, upload timestamp, and optional expire_at/description) as admin. Verify that correct attachment is created with proper validation for file type, size, duplicate hash, and required fields. Edge cases: missing required field (expect error), invalid owner_type or mime_type, duplicate hash_sha256 (should return descriptive error), and unauthorized user attempt. Validate audit trail on creation.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin with permissions to create attachments.

scenarios.draft: Test updating mutable metadata fields of an existing attachment as an admin. Confirm ability to change ownership context, expiration, and business description according to business rules. Attempt updates that violate business rules, such as changing immutable fields (storage_uri, hash_sha256), transitioning to restricted owner_type, or setting invalid value for retention policy (expect descriptive errors). Edge cases include updating a non-existent or soft deleted attachment, as well as unauthorized update attempt.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin for authorization.
Create an attachment to update.

scenarios.draft: Test soft deleting an attachment as an admin. Verify that the deleted_at field is set, the attachment is omitted from standard queries, and that audit logs are updated for compliance. Attempt to delete a non-existent, already soft-deleted, or unauthorized attachment (should yield descriptive errors). Ensure that business references to deleted attachments are enforced (cannot be referenced, or trigger appropriate errors if in use), and that only admin or privileged users can perform the deletion.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin with permissions to perform attachment deletions.
Create an attachment to be deleted.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieval of a specific customer history event using /customer/customers/{customerId}/histories/{historyId}. The scenario checks that the owner customer can retrieve their own history event in full detail, including event type, before/after values, actor, timestamp, and context. Ensure that correct data is returned for valid and active records (not soft-deleted). Also, test that unauthorized access (other customers or anonymous users) is denied with an appropriate error. Edge cases: request non-existing or soft-deleted historyId, and verify appropriate error handling.

dependencies.purpose: Create an authenticated customer to perform the lookup operation.
List available history records to obtain a valid historyId.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin can retrieve the full details of a customer's specific history event by customerId and historyId, including event type, actor, before/after values, and timestamps. Verify successful retrieval when the record exists and is not soft-deleted. Validate that the API enforces admin-only access, blocking regular customers from using this route, returning a proper error. Scenario should cover non-existent and soft-deleted historyId as error cases with correct error codes.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate an admin for API access.
Register a sample customer account for history lookup.
List customer's history to capture a valid historyId for detail lookup.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin can paginate, filter, and sort the list of sellers using the /admin/sellers PATCH endpoint. Include filtering by company name, status (pending, active, suspended), registration window, and email verification state. Validate correct paging, proper search results with relevant seller meta data, and proper enforcement that only admin users can access this endpoint. Also, test that permission errors are returned for non-admin users. Edge cases: empty result sets, malformed filters, and invalid paging parameters should all deliver proper error handling.

dependencies.purpose: Register/admin login to perform the API call.
Register one or more seller accounts for presence in the search results.

scenarios.draft: Validate that searching sellers with a filter that matches no results (for example, using a non-existent company name or date range) returns an empty paginated response and does not fail. Ensure pagination meta information is correctly shown even with zero results, and that the status code is still success (not error).

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as admin to perform search operations.

scenarios.draft: Verify that an authenticated seller can use the /seller/sellers/{sellerId} endpoint to view the complete details of their own profile, including business/identity fields, status, KYC, verification, and timestamps. The test should also verify that sellers cannot access another seller's profile (should receive an authorization error). Include negative cases: not-found for deleted or missing sellerId, and masked fields for unauthorized users.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate a seller for test operations.

scenarios.draft: Test that an authenticated admin can use /admin/sellers/{sellerId} to retrieve a seller's full profile, including all business and verification data. Ensure all sensitive fields are visible to admins only, and that access is denied to non-admins. Failure scenarios: request a non-existent or deleted sellerId and verify correct error codes. Also check that field security does not over-expose or under-expose information based on admin privileges.

dependencies.purpose: Obtain admin authentication for API access.
Create seller accounts to supply a valid sellerId for test.

scenarios.draft: Update a product-channel mapping's attributes as an admin. First, create a product entity and a channel entity using their respective creation endpoints. Then, map the product to the channel by creating a product-channel mapping. Update this mapping by changing attributes such as status, business context, or auxiliary metadata, ensuring the endpoint reflects the changes. Return and verify the updated mapping details contain new values. This tests that admins can correct or adjust exposure or business rules across channels for an existing product.

dependencies.purpose: Create a product to be mapped to a channel.
Create a channel to link with the product.
Create the initial product-channel mapping to be updated by this test.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to update a product-channel mapping for a combination of productId and productChannelMapId that does not exist. The test verifies that the endpoint returns an appropriate error message and does not create any new mapping. This is essential to confirm error handling and compliance in cases of stale or incorrect references.

dependencies.purpose: Create a product to provide a valid productId, ensuring only the mappingId is non-existent.

scenarios.draft: Perform a soft-delete on an active product-channel mapping as the product's seller. The test must first register a seller account and log them in, create a new product via the seller API, create a valid channel (admin action), and map the product to the channel as the seller. Then, execute a DELETE for the mapping. Confirm that the mapping is removed from active queries (i.e., set deleted_at), but remains in compliance/audit evidence. This covers the business need to selectively remove products from certain channels without data loss.

dependencies.purpose: Register a seller account with valid credentials.
Authenticate as the seller to obtain JWT for authorization.
Create the product to be mapped to a channel by the seller.
Create a channel entity to be used for mapping.
Create a product-channel mapping to be deleted in this flow.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to soft-delete a product-channel mapping that was already previously deleted (soft-deleted). After successful deletion, a second DELETE should return an appropriate not-found or idempotent response, confirming endpoint robustness and proper idempotency for resource removals.

dependencies.purpose: Register a seller account for the scenario.
Login to obtain seller authorization.
Create product entity as seller.
Create channel via admin for mapping.
Create product-channel mapping to delete.
First delete to simulate already-deleted state.

scenarios.draft: Delete (soft/hard as applicable) a product-channel mapping using admin privileges. This scenario covers the business need for admin to force-remove a mapping for moderation, compliance, or curation purposes. Ensure a product and channel are created, create the mapping, and then delete as admin. Verify that the mapping is no longer available in active search and is retained for audit, as per soft-delete logic. The admin perspective is important for compliance and high-level curation functions.

dependencies.purpose: Create a product to be linked with a channel.
Create a business channel for mapping.
Create the product-channel mapping to be deleted in this test.

scenarios.draft: Test the ability to retrieve a paginated, filtered, and sorted list of point wallet transaction histories as an admin. Include scenarios where filters are used for wallet, transaction_type, date range, and actor; verify that only authorized admin access is allowed. Successful tests should return appropriately filtered/paginated results. Failure scenarios include malformed filters and unauthorized access attempts, both of which must return appropriate error responses. Also test for empty result sets when queries do not match any records.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new customer point wallet to serve as the basis for searching and assigning point transactions.
Insert one or more transaction histories with known properties for search and pagination testing.

scenarios.draft: Test fetching the details of a single point wallet transaction history record by its pointHistoryId as an admin. Begin by creating a point wallet and a corresponding transaction, then attempt a successful retrieval. Also, include negative scenarios such as attempting to access a non-existent transaction or using an invalid/deleted pointHistoryId. Unauthorized access by non-admin roles must result in error. All accesses should trigger audit logging.

dependencies.purpose: Set up a customer point wallet to which transactions will be added.
Create a transaction history record to be read by its ID in this scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test creating a new point wallet transaction history as an admin, ensuring all required fields are validated and properly persisted. Success scenario involves providing valid wallet and transaction data, receiving the created transaction object, and verifying its audit attributes. Also test failure scenarios: 1) missing or invalid required fields (such as invalid wallet reference), 2) violation of business logic (e.g., recording a transaction against a non-existent wallet), and 3) ensuring audit logs capture creation. If attempting to create a duplicate transaction or out-of-bounds adjustment, an explicit error must be returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create the point wallet needed as a reference to attach a new history transaction.

scenarios.draft: Test updating allowed fields for a specific point wallet transaction (pointHistoryId) as an admin. Start by creating a wallet and an associated transaction, then update mutable fields (such as remarks or admin logs). Attempt both valid updates and prohibited updates (such as trying to change immutable core transaction attributes). Unauthorized, invalid update or reference to a non-existing transaction should yield proper errors. All changes must be audit-logged.

dependencies.purpose: Create a point wallet to associate with the transaction history.
Create a point transaction record that can be updated in the test.

scenarios.draft: Test the soft-delete operation for a point wallet transaction history by pointHistoryId as an admin. First, create a wallet and a transaction. Successfully deleting should set the deleted_at field, preserve the record for audit, and remove it from active queries. Attempting to delete an already deleted or non-existent history should result in an appropriate success or error response (idempotency or not found). Also ensure that all operations trigger audit logs for compliance.

dependencies.purpose: Create the customer point wallet needed for the transaction history.
Insert a valid transaction record that will be deleted during the test.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving detailed information for a specific product content (such as an image, video, or document) by its unique productContentId under the given productId as a seller. First, ensure a seller account exists and is authenticated. Next, create a product, then add content (e.g., image) to the product. Attempt to retrieve the content's detail as the owner seller, expecting full access to all fields defined in the response. Also include a scenario where a different seller or an unauthorized role attempts access, confirming proper error handling for forbidden access or not found errors.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new seller account to act as the product owner.
Seller creates a new product to which content will be attached.
Add a content entry to the product to set up productContentId.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin can fetch the complete detail of a product content by providing valid productId and productContentId. First, create a product and add product content via an authenticated seller. Then, attempt to retrieve this content as an admin and verify that all content fields (including status, content_uri, content_type, etc.) are returned. Also, cover error handling for invalid IDs (product not found or content not found) and soft-deleted content (verify the correct error is returned).

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin account for authorization to fetch content details.
Register a seller for product/content creation, as only sellers can initially add products and content.
Seller creates a new product.
Add a content record to the product for test retrieval by admin.

scenarios.draft: Test creating a new product content item (e.g., adding an image or video) for a specified product as a seller. Steps: Register a seller, create a product, then submit a valid product content creation payload (content_type, content_uri, ordering, status). Validate successful creation with all required fields. Test validation errors for missing required fields, invalid content_type, or malformed content_uri. Also test business rule violation such as attempting to add duplicate content with same ordering for the same product.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate as a seller.
Create the owning product for content creation.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin can create new product content for a specified product. First, set up an admin account and ensure a product exists. Attempt to create product content with valid fields as admin. Validate success and check that the record is associated correctly. Also, test error scenarios: creating content for a non-existent product (should fail with not found) and providing invalid/missing required fields (should yield validation errors).

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin account for admin-privileged content creation.
Register a seller to create the base product.
Create a product as seller (since only sellers can register products).

scenarios.draft: Test updating an existing product content entity (such as correcting its content_type, updating its description, or changing its status) as the owning seller. First, create a seller and a product, then add a content entity to it. Next, issue a valid update as the owner seller and validate the changes. Additionally, cover negative scenarios where update is attempted with invalid data (violating schema or business rules), or by a different (non-owner) seller, confirming permission denial. Also test update on soft-deleted content (should result in not found or error).

dependencies.purpose: Register a seller for full content lifecycle tests.
Create a new product to act as parent for the content resource.
Create the content entity to obtain a productContentId for updating.

scenarios.draft: Test that a seller can retrieve full details of a specific product bundle that they own. The scenario should create a seller and a product under that seller, then add a product bundle to the product. The test will call the GET endpoint to fetch this bundle by its productId and productBundleId, verifying all fields (name, description, price, bundle contents, metadata) are returned and correspond to expected values. Permission and ownership checks must be covered.

dependencies.purpose: Register a seller account for authentication and ownership.
Create a product under the seller, to which bundles can be attached.
Create the product bundle under the product, establishing the required productBundleId.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin user can access the complete details for a specific product bundle under any product, regardless of seller ownership. Set up a product and bundle as a seller, then authenticate as admin and attempt to retrieve the bundle's details by productId and productBundleId. Validate all schema fields and ensure the response includes even non-public admin metadata if expected. Missing or unauthorized access must return appropriate errors.

dependencies.purpose: Register (or authenticate) an admin user for privileged access.
Register a seller to create a product and bundle for testing purposes.
Create a product as the test seller, required for bundle association.
Create a product bundle under the created product so there is a bundle to fetch.

scenarios.draft: Test that a seller can successfully create a product bundle for one of their own products. The scenario should include registering a seller, creating a product, and then issuing a request to create a bundle. Verify that bundle creation fails if required attributes are missing or if the seller attempts to create the bundle under a product they don't own. Validate returned fields upon creation and ensure audit metadata is recorded. Attempt to create a duplicate bundle and expect a validation error.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate the seller for creating entities.
Set up a product to which a bundle will be added.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin can create a product bundle on behalf of any product in the system. Set up a product as a seller, then authenticate as an admin and attempt to create a product bundle under the productId. Verify that admin permissions suffice, returned information matches expectations, and all required fields are enforced. Test creation failure when required fields are omitted or referential integrity fails (e.g., using invalid productId).

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate an admin for privileged product and bundle management.
Register a seller to create a product which the admin can use for bundle testing.
Create a product as this seller for the admin to assign a bundle to.

scenarios.draft: Test that a seller can update the details of an existing product bundle they own. The flow should create a seller, a product, a bundle, then update the bundle's name, description, status, or price using this endpoint. Validate that updates are applied and reflected in subsequent GET responses. If a seller attempts to update a bundle for a product they don't own, verify that an unauthorized error is returned. Invalid updates (such as missing required fields or failed validation) must also be tested and confirmed to fail with meaningful errors.

dependencies.purpose: Register a seller for product/bundle management.
Create a product for bundle testing.
Create an initial product bundle before attempting update.

scenarios.draft: Verify that an administrator can successfully update a product tag's attributes (such as the tag string or metadata) for a valid product and tag ID. First, ensure a product and at least one product tag exists by creating them if necessary. Then, perform a valid update operation, and confirm that the tag's data is modified accordingly in the response.

dependencies.purpose: Create a product to which the tag will be attached.
Add an initial tag to the product to set up for tag update.

scenarios.draft: Test updating a tag for a non-existent product or productTagId. Attempt an update with invalid IDs and confirm that the operation fails with a not found error indicating the tag or product is missing.

Validate that an unauthorized user (non-admin or lacking appropriate permissions) cannot update a product tag. Attempt to perform a tag update without admin credentials, expecting a permission denied error with an appropriate message.

Verify that a seller is able to successfully delete (remove or soft-delete) a specific tag from their own product. The test must first create a seller account, a product owned by that seller, and then a tag on that product. After setup, the seller should delete the tag and verify that the tag is removed (e.g., via list/search endpoint or by absence on get).

dependencies.purpose: Register a new seller account who will own the product.
Create a product under the seller's ownership.
Add a tag to the seller's product for deletion test.

scenarios.draft: Try to delete a tag from a product as a seller using non-existent productId or productTagId, and confirm the error message or code reflects resource not found. No deletion should occur in this scenario.

Attempt to delete a tag from another seller's product and assert that the operation fails with an appropriate permission denied or forbidden error. This ensures that sellers can only manage tags on their own products.

dependencies.purpose: Register a second seller who will attempt the unauthorized deletion.
A product owned by the first seller with a tag, which the second seller will try to delete.

scenarios.draft: Ensure that an admin can delete (remove or soft-delete) a specific tag from any product. After setting up a product and attaching a tag, perform the delete as an admin and verify via search or get that the tag is no longer present or is properly soft-deleted.

dependencies.purpose: Create a product as setup target for tagging and deletion.
Attach a tag to the product as a setup step.

scenarios.draft: Test deletion of a tag for an invalid productId or productTagId by admin and verify that it returns an error signifying that the resource does not exist. No side effects should occur.
Attempt to perform a tag delete as a non-admin account. The test should ensure that only authorized admin users can perform this action and that unauthorized attempts are rejected with a clear error.

As a seller, retrieve a paginated and filtered list of search keywords assigned to one of their products. Set up by creating a seller, a product, and several search keywords for it. Execute the search (with and without filters such as keyword string, pagination, etc.) and verify the response contains the expected search keyword entries and metadata.

dependencies.purpose: Create a seller account to use throughout this workflow.
Create a product for the seller.
Add several keywords to the product to enable meaningful search.

scenarios.draft: Search for keywords on a seller product that has no keywords attached and verify the result is an empty set (validating pagination and edge case handling). This confirms the search endpoint gracefully handles products with no keywords.

dependencies.purpose: Create a seller for product setup.
Create a product with no attached search keywords yet.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to search keywords on a product not owned by the seller and assert that the operation fails with a permission denied or forbidden error. This verifies that sellers are restricted to their own products' data.

dependencies.purpose: Register a second seller who will attempt to search another seller's product.
Create a product owned by a different seller.

scenarios.draft: As an administrator, perform a paginated and filtered search of search keywords for a specific product. Prepare by creating a product with multiple keywords and then perform the keyword search with various filters (e.g., by keyword string, status, or use pagination). Validate that all assigned keywords are retrievable and filters work as expected.

dependencies.purpose: Create a product that will have search keywords attached.
Attach multiple keywords to the product to set up for keyword search.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to search for keywords for a non-existent product (invalid productId) as admin. Verify the operation fails gracefully, returning an appropriate error that the product is not found.
Attempt to search search keywords as a non-admin or unauthorized user. Confirm the system forbids access and presents a permission denied error.

Test successful soft deletion of a customer profile by an admin. First, an admin user registers, logs in, and creates a customer account (with separate profile). The admin then soft deletes the customer's profile via this endpoint and verifies that the profile is hidden from business processes but retained for audit (via customer_histories). Attempts to fetch this profile after deletion must fail or indicate non-existence. Confirm the customer cannot log in or perform business actions after soft deletion. Audit the action in customer_histories to validate compliance logging.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin account to perform administrative actions.
Authenticate as admin to acquire authorization for privileged operations.
Register a new customer account to be soft-deleted.

scenarios.draft: Test soft delete failure when attempting to delete a customer profile that is already soft-deleted. First, an admin creates and then soft deletes a customer profile. The admin then attempts to delete the same customer profile again. The system must return an appropriate error response indicating that the customer does not exist or is already deleted.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin for the test.
Authenticate as admin.
Register a new customer to delete.
Delete the customer before retrying deletion to simulate double-deletion.

scenarios.draft: Test the scenario where a customer successfully soft deletes their own profile. First, a customer registers and logs in. The customer then sends a request to delete their own profile. Afterwards, verify the account cannot be used to log in and is absent from listings, but the audit log in customer_histories remains intact for compliance. Ensure all related addresses and resources remain unaffected unless otherwise specified.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new customer for the account self-deletion scenario.
Authenticate the customer prior to self-initiated deletion.

scenarios.draft: Test error handling when a customer attempts to soft-delete their profile after it has already been deleted. Register and log in as a customer, delete the profile, and attempt to delete it again. The response must indicate the customer is already deleted or not found, preventing redundant operations.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new customer.
Authenticate as the customer.
Delete the customer profile prior to attempting double deletion.

scenarios.draft: Test admin's ability to fetch a paginated and filtered list of addresses for a specific customer. First, an admin account is created and logged in, as well as a customer with multiple addresses linked. The admin uses this endpoint with various filters (e.g., city, state, is_primary) and pagination parameters to list and search the customer's addresses. Confirm only addresses meeting filter criteria are returned, and pagination works as expected. Verify that addresses for non-existent customerId yield the proper error.

dependencies.purpose: Establish admin privileges for the operation.
Authenticate the admin for subsequent actions.
Register a new customer to create addresses for.
Create several addresses for the test customer before listing and filtering.

scenarios.draft: Test the scenario where a logged-in customer retrieves their own active addresses using diverse filters and pagination. First, register and log in as a customer and create multiple addresses. Fetch paginated addresses, applying filters such as alias, is_primary, or city. Confirm only the customer's addresses are returned and privacy is enforced (no access to other customers' addresses). Also, test edge case of querying with an invalid or unauthorized customerId to ensure privacy is not breached and errors are returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create a customer account for the self-address listing scenario.
Obtain a customer session/auth token.
Create addresses for the customer before listing.

scenarios.draft: Test the ability of an admin to successfully fetch a specific customer address using customerId and addressId. First, an admin registers and logs in, creates a customer, then adds an address for that customer. The admin fetches the newly created address by ID and verifies all fields are returned. Next, test that fetching a non-existent or unauthorized address (wrong customerId/addressId pair) returns a proper error. Also confirm that admins cannot access addresses of already-deleted customers.

dependencies.purpose: Register admin to authorize the retrieval.
Log in as admin for access rights.
Register a new customer for the test.
Create an address for the customer before fetching it.

scenarios.draft: Test successful retrieval of a product option's details by an admin. First, create a product as an admin, then add a product option to this product, and finally as an admin user, request the details for the specific option using its productId and productOptionId. Confirm that the response includes all expected product option fields and observes data masking/visibility as per admin role.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new product as an admin to provide a valid productId.
Add a product option to the product to obtain a valid productOptionId.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieval failure when requesting a nonexistent product option. As an admin, attempt to retrieve a product option using a productId and productOptionId pair that do not exist or are not linked. Expect a not found error with the appropriate status code and message.

Test access control by attempting to fetch a product option's details as a non-admin or non-authorized user. This should result in a permission denied error, demonstrating enforcement of role-based access control. No product creation required, as the focus is unauthorized access.

Test successful creation of a new product option by a seller for their own product. Register a seller, log in, create a product as the seller, then attempt to create a product option under this product. Validate that all required fields and business logic constraints are enforced, and that the result returns expected data.

dependencies.purpose: Register a seller account to obtain valid credentials.
Obtain seller JWT for authenticated actions.
Create a product as the seller, providing a valid productId.

scenarios.draft: Test failure when attempting to create a product option with a duplicate SKU under the same product as a seller. Ensure the first product option is created successfully, then create a second with the same SKU and expect a validation error for duplicate constraint.

dependencies.purpose: Register a seller account for authentication.
Get JWT for seller session.
Create a seller's product for option association.
Create the first product option and get the SKU for duplication.

scenarios.draft: Test that invalid input (missing required fields or invalid field formats) is properly rejected when a seller attempts to create a product option. Attempt creation with missing or malformed data and verify the system returns the correct validation error messages.

dependencies.purpose: Register a seller to get credentials.
Authenticate as a seller.
Provide a product context for the product option.

scenarios.draft: Test successful product option creation by an admin for an existing product.
