scenarios.draft: Test requesting details for a channel that does not exist or has already been soft deleted. Validate that the system returns the appropriate 404 error and compliance code, and that no sensitive data is exposed in the error. The test covers non-existent UUIDs, soft-deleted channel records, and audit compliance.

dependencies.purpose: Obtain admin authorization.
Create and acquire a channelId, then soft-delete it to set up the not-found/soft-deleted scenario.
Perform soft-delete of the channel before detail query.

scenarios.draft: Test that a non-admin (customer or seller) receives a permission error when attempting to retrieve details of a specific channel. The system should enforce RBAC controls, returning an error code and not exposing channel metadata.

dependencies.purpose: Create a customer account and JWT token for the unauthorized access scenario.
Create a channel to obtain a valid channelId for permission test.

scenarios.draft: Test successful creation of a new business channel by an authorized admin user. Include all required business fields: unique code, name, activation status, and optional branding/logo/description. After creation, verify the response matches the request and auditing is properly logged. Attempt to create a duplicate code to ensure proper error is returned (see duplicate test case).

dependencies.purpose: Obtain administrator session for creation rights.

scenarios.draft: Test handling of duplicate channel code on creation. First, create a new channel with a unique code. Then, attempt to create another channel with the same code and verify that the system rejects this with a conflict or validation error, as code is globally unique. The test checks for correct error response and the absence of side effects.

dependencies.purpose: Login as admin to gain create rights.
Create the first channel with a unique code to set up conflict scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test rejection of channel creation requests with missing required fields or business rule violations (e.g., empty name, code not unique, invalid data type). Validate the correct validation error is returned as per compliance requirements and no partial entries are created.

dependencies.purpose: Admin login for permission.

scenarios.draft: Test that non-admin or unauthenticated users are denied access to create new channels. Attempt channel creation as a customer, seller, or without credentials and verify that access is blocked with an error code and that no data is created or changed.

dependencies.purpose: Register a customer account to test unauthorized scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test a successful update of channel fields, such as name, logo, and description, by an admin. Code field is immutable and attempts to update it should fail. After updating, verify the updated_at timestamp changes, audit logs are created, and the response data reflects changes. Confirm that updates to valid, non-deleted channel IDs proceed as expected.

dependencies.purpose: Admin session for update operation.
Create a channel to update and extract channelId.

scenarios.draft: Test that updates attempting to change the channel code are rejected. Attempt to update the code during PUT; the system should deny the request with an error and audit the attempt. Confirm code immutability in practice.

dependencies.purpose: Admin login for request authorization.
Create the initial channel for update scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test that updating a non-existent or already soft-deleted channel returns a not-found error and no changes are made. First, create and soft-delete a channel, then attempt to update it. Validate correct error responses and compliance logs.

dependencies.purpose: Admin login.
Create a channel and obtain channelId.
Soft-delete the channel to set up test condition.

scenarios.draft: Test denial of update attempts by non-admin users. Attempt a channel update as a customer, seller, or unauthenticated session and verify that the system enforces RBAC by blocking the operation and returning appropriate error responses.

dependencies.purpose: Register as customer user to simulate non-admin update attempt.
Create a channel for use in the permission test.

scenarios.draft: Test successful soft deletion of a channel record by admin, ensuring the deleted_at timestamp is set and the channel is no longer returned in standard searches. After deletion, verify audit logs and exclusion from normal queries. This ensures compliance and business traceability policies are met.

dependencies.purpose: Admin login for delete access.
Create the channel to acquire channelId for deletion.

scenarios.draft: Test attempting to soft-delete a channel that is already soft-deleted or does not exist. Confirm that the API returns the appropriate not found or idempotent error and that audit chains are properly updated.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as admin.
Create a new channel to obtain the channelId.
Perform initial soft-delete.

scenarios.draft: Test rejection of soft-delete attempts by unauthorized (non-admin) users. Ensure that deletion is not permitted and error response includes appropriate compliance/audit code.

dependencies.purpose: Register a regular customer to use for an unauthorized deletion attempt.
Create a channel whose channelId will be used in the unauthorized delete test.

scenarios.draft: Test appeal creation by a seller against a moderation event. Scenario includes valid appeal creation for a moderation event the seller is involved in, requiring prior moderation event existence. Verify appeal is linked to the seller and correct moderation event, and ensure response includes appeal metadata and audit trail. Additionally, attempt to create a duplicate appeal for the same event and verify that the API rejects the duplicate with an appropriate error message and code. Verify error messages for unauthorized or policy-violating attempts (e.g., seller tries to appeal an unrelated event).

dependencies.purpose: Register a seller in order to obtain credentials for authentication and to submit an appeal.
Authenticate as the seller to obtain a JWT for authorized appeal actions.
Create a moderation event record as the target for the seller's appeal. This must precede the appeal submission.

scenarios.draft: Test direct creation of an appeal via admin for any moderation event. The scenario includes issuing an admin-created appeal for a moderation event and for an event where the admin is not the appellant. Validate the link between the appeal and the correct moderation event. Verify that unauthorized creation or attempts with invalid references return error codes. Test that attempts to create duplicate appeals for the same event are rejected according to system constraints.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin to enable admin-level operations.
Log in as admin to acquire authorization for creating appeals.
Create at least one moderation event to serve as a target for the admin appeal creation.

scenarios.draft: Test updating an existing appeal as an admin. Scenario includes updating the status (e.g., approve, reject, escalate), decision comment, and outcome fields. Validate that updating is allowed only by authorized admins and that business rules like permanent closure after final decision are enforced. Attempt to update an immutable or already-closed appeal and verify that rejection occurs with appropriate error messaging. Confirm compliant audit log entries are generated.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin to obtain credentials for authorized update operations.
Log in as admin to acquire authorization.
Create a moderation event to associate with an appeal.
Create the initial appeal record that will be updated in this test.

scenarios.draft: Test soft deletion of an appeal by an admin. Scenario includes deleting an appeal and verifying the deleted_at timestamp is set. Test that attempting to delete a non-existent or already deleted appeal returns a not-found or appropriate error response. Confirm that, after deletion, the appeal is unavailable via standard queries but is present for audit purposes. Ensure delete actions are traceable in compliance logs.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin for delete permissions.
Log in as admin to acquire delete rights.
Provision a moderation event for appeal linkage.
Create the appeal record that will be soft-deleted during this scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test paginated and filtered retrieval of customer's favorite products. Scenario includes: creating a customer, authenticating, favoriting multiple products, and then retrieving the favorite products list using pagination and filters (e.g., filter by product attribute, favorited date). Validate that only the authenticated customer can access their favorites, and that pagination metadata is correct. Attempt access with an unauthorized user and verify proper access denial. Ensure the response includes product details along with favoriting metadata, and verify security by ensuring that favorites of other users are inaccessible.

dependencies.purpose: Register a customer to enable favorite product actions and for authentication context.
Authenticate as a customer to obtain a JWT for further authorized actions.
Create products to be favorited by the customer; ensures realistic product data for the test.
Favorite products for the customer so there is at least one favorite to retrieve in the list.

scenarios.draft: Retrieve a specific product-to-channel mapping for a product as a seller. Validate that proper details (mapping info, channel context, audit/status fields) are fully returned when the mapping exists and the seller owns the product. Dependencies: product and mapping creation required first.

dependencies.purpose: Create a product for the seller account to use as owner context.
Create a channel mapping for the product which will later be retrieved by productChannelMapId.

scenarios.draft: As an admin, retrieve the details of a specific product-channel mapping by both productId and productChannelMapId. Test for successful retrieval with comprehensive mapping and channel fields and verify admin can access mappings for any product-channel pairing in the system. Ensure the mapping exists before retrieval.

dependencies.purpose: Create a product as an admin to serve as a mapping parent.
Establish a channel mapping which can be looked up in this test.

scenarios.draft: Test a seller creating a new mapping from a product to a business channel. Validate that mapping is successful with unique combination, required channel, and that audit trails are persisted. Validate error behavior for attempts to create duplicate mappings, link to non-existent channels/products, or link a product not owned by the seller.

dependencies.purpose: Create a product under the seller to use in channel mapping.
Create a business channel so it can be mapped to a product.

scenarios.draft: Test an admin creating a product-channel mapping entry for an arbitrary product. Validate successful creation, enforcement of uniqueness, and error handling on duplicates or invalid references. Audit logging must be verified for compliance. Includes negative case: attempt to map with duplicate channel/product pairing results in error code.

dependencies.purpose: Create a product as context for admin mapping.
Create a channel that admin can map to a product.

scenarios.draft: Test that a seller can update a product-channel mapping (e.g., status or metadata changes) only on their own products. Check successful update and proper audit trace. Validation: only allowed fields can be changed, edits on mappings for products not owned by the seller should be forbidden. Verify business rules: updating to same channel on different mapping is disallowed as duplicate; invalid product or channel ID yields error.

dependencies.purpose: Seller creates product as context.
Create a valid mapping entry which can then be updated.

scenarios.draft: Test searching error logs with a variety of filter conditions and with pagination. First, prepare a set of error log entries with varying error codes, severity, entity association, and timestamps (if log creation endpoint available; otherwise, pre-seeded data is assumed). As an admin user, perform a PATCH request with representative filters—such as time window, errorCode, severity, and sort order—and validate that the paginated response matches only the expected filtered set of error logs. Edge cases include providing invalid filter parameters, requesting an empty result set, and attempting the operation with insufficient admin privileges, all of which must trigger relevant error responses or not found returns. Ensure pagination fields (page, pageSize) are respected and total counts align with query results.

dependencies.purpose: Obtain a valid admin JWT token required for authentication to access error logs. This establishes an authenticated admin session for the test.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving detailed information of an error log by errorLogId for both success and failure cases. As an admin, fetch the details for a known valid error logId and verify all expected fields are present (error code, message, stack/context, severity, root cause, timestamps, etc). Attempt to retrieve an error log with a random or already deleted logId and validate that an appropriate not found error is returned. Also, simulate requesting with a valid errorLogId but as a non-admin user to confirm that access is denied. All data returned must match the values in the backend, and any access should be fully audit logged.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as admin and retrieve JWT for authorization in error log detail requests.
Search and obtain a valid errorLogId for use in the successful retrieval test. Ensures that the error log being fetched exists.

scenarios.draft: Test advanced audit log searches using multiple filters (action type, actor, entity, time range, description) and pagination, exercised by an authorized admin user. Setup must include relevant audit log entries (Create, Update, Delete actions by various admin actors on different entities). Perform a PATCH request using multi-filters and validate the result contains only audit logs that satisfy all filter conditions. Attempt search with invalid parameters to check validation error handling. Also, test search with no matching results and verify an empty list. Finally, verify that unauthorized users are prevented from accessing this endpoint.

dependencies.purpose: Establish admin authentication and get JWT for audit log queries.

scenarios.draft: Validate retrieval of a specific audit log detail using auditLogId by an admin user. Confirm that all critical audit information is returned, including actor, action, timestamp, target entity, and before/after state when available. Test edge cases by accessing a non-existent, deleted, or unauthorized auditLogId and verify accurate error or permission-denied response. Data integrity is critical—field values in the response must match the log record as originally written, and all requests must be properly logged for compliance evidence.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as admin to gain access to audit log records.
Search existing audit logs to identify a valid auditLogId for successful detail retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Test the full customer registration flow, focusing on email uniqueness and password policy business rules. First, register as a new customer with a unique email, password, name, and required profile information, and verify a JWT token and newly created customer details are returned, with audit events recorded in customer_histories. Next, attempt to register a customer using the same email twice, and confirm that the API responds with an error indicating duplicate email constraint violation. Validate that passwords are hashed and not returned in any response. Also, attempt registration with malformed input, missing required fields, or weak password and expect clear validation errors. All successful and failed attempts should be audit-logged for compliance.

Test admin login with both valid and invalid credentials. First, with correct email and password, ensure JWT is issued and admin profile fields are returned, with login event logged for compliance. Then, use wrong password or non-existing email and verify that authentication is rejected with specific error codes and no JWT is issued. Also, test login for a locked or soft-deleted admin and expect an appropriate denial. All login attempts, both successful and failed, should be audited.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin account with known credentials for controlled login attempts. This ensures deterministic results for various login scenarios.

scenarios.draft: Test the ability of an admin to soft-delete a mileage transaction for a given wallet and transaction ID. Prepare a mileage wallet and a set of mileage transactions as prerequisites. Ensure that deleting a transaction sets the appropriate deleted_at timestamp without removing the record from the database. After deletion, verify that the transaction can no longer be accessed via normal queries but is retained for audit/compliance. Attempting to delete an already deleted or non-existent transaction must return an error. Also confirm that audit logs capture the delete operation for future reference.

dependencies.purpose: Create a mileage wallet for a test customer to serve as the parent entity for transaction creation.
Create a mileage transaction to be targeted for deletion in this scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test the product inquiry search endpoint for a customer, focusing on applying advanced filters, full-text search, and pagination. Ensure the customer can retrieve only their own inquiries, and searching by fields such as product ID, title keyword, status, and date range yields correct results. Validate that attempting to use unauthorized filters or requesting data not owned by the customer returns appropriate errors. Ensure that result pagination works and summary data is returned in line with UI requirements.

dependencies.purpose: Register a customer to execute product inquiry searches as an authenticated user.
Create one or more product inquiries under the customer for realistic search results.

scenarios.draft: Test the product inquiry search for a seller, verifying that the seller can filter and retrieve inquiries related only to products they own. Apply search by various product IDs, title/body keywords, AI flag thresholds, public status, and created date. Check that pagination and correct sorting work as expected. Attempting to access inquiries for products not owned by the seller should fail or yield empty results. Unauthorized filter usage should trigger error responses. Additionally, confirm that audit logs include query history.

dependencies.purpose: Register a seller account to ensure role-based filtering of product inquiries works.
Create product inquiries targeting products owned by the seller to populate search results.

scenarios.draft: Test the admin's ability to perform a system-wide advanced search over product inquiries. Validate support for multiple statuses (published, draft, blocked), product/customer IDs, keyword search, AI moderation flags, date windows, and public/private distinctions. Pagination and sorting should deliver deterministic results. Attempts with malformed or invalid filters return clear error responses. Confirm the audit log records both the search criteria and access due to compliance needs.

dependencies.purpose: Create and authenticate an admin account to test privileged search permissions.
Generate several product inquiries with different customers/products/statuses to provide data for admin-level search coverage.

scenarios.draft: Test fetching full detail of a product inquiry as the customer owner. Ensure the returned data includes all fields (customer, product, content, status, AI analysis fields, etc.). Attempt to access a non-existent productInquiryId or one belonging to another customer should return a permission error or 404. The scenario also covers verifying compliance with privacy and field-level access controls for the customer role. Audit logging for inquiry access is also checked.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate a customer who will act as inquiry owner.
Create a product inquiry for the customer to be fetched in the detail view test.

scenarios.draft: Test successful admin login with valid credentials. Register a new admin using the registration endpoint with a unique email and password, then perform a login using those credentials. Confirm the response includes a valid JWT token in the Authorization header and the admin profile, and all compliance logging is correctly triggered.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin account as a prerequisite to obtain credentials for login testing.

scenarios.draft: Test failed admin login due to invalid password. Register a new admin, then attempt to log in with the correct email but an incorrect password. Verify that the API returns an error indicating invalid credentials and that no JWT token is provided. Ensure proper audit logging of the failed login attempt.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin account to have a known valid email for login.

scenarios.draft: Test failed admin login with a non-existent email address. Attempt to log in with an email address that does not exist in the system and any password value. Verify the API returns an appropriate error (such as user not found or unauthorized), and ensure that error logging and compliance requirements are met.

Test successful logout of an authenticated admin session. Register and log in as a new admin to obtain a valid JWT, then perform a logout. Confirm that the session is invalidated, subsequent API calls with the same token fail authorization, and audit log entries for logout are created.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin to prepare a valid session for logout.
Authenticate as admin to get valid JWT for logout test.

scenarios.draft: Test logout attempt without valid authentication. Call the logout endpoint without a valid JWT or with an expired/invalid token. Verify API returns an error indicating there is no active session to log out, and that compliance/audit log reflects the attempt.

Test successful validation of a valid JWT token for admin. Register and log in as an admin to obtain a JWT, then validate the token. Ensure the endpoint confirms authorization status, returns session/profile info, and records audit logs for token validation actions.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new admin account for token generation.
Login to obtain a valid JWT token for validation.

scenarios.draft: Test failed validation of an invalid or expired admin JWT token. Attempt to validate a clearly invalid or expired JWT token and verify that the API rejects it with proper error messages and auditing.

Test successful change of admin password. Register and log in as a new admin to obtain a valid session. Change the password using the correct current password and a new secure password. Verify the system updates the password, returns a success message, audit logs the change, and invalidates all previous sessions.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin account for conducting password changes.
Authenticate as admin to perform password change with valid session.

scenarios.draft: Test failure to change password when the current password is incorrect. Register and log in as admin, then attempt a password change, providing an incorrect current password. Confirm the operation fails, password is not changed, a detailed error/code is returned, and an audit entry is created.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin account and acquire credentials.
Authenticate to get a valid session for the operation.

scenarios.draft: Test successful registration of a new seller account. Provide unique email, valid password, and all required company profile information (company name, business number, representative name, etc.). Confirm that the account is created, JWT tokens are issued in the response headers, onboarding audit and compliance events are logged, and that follow-up login will succeed with these credentials.

Test failure to register a seller when the email already exists. Register a seller with a specific email, then attempt a second registration with the same email. Confirm the API rejects the request with a duplicate email error, does not create a new account, and returns precise error feedback for the user as well as audit/compliance logs.

dependencies.purpose: First registration to establish a duplicate candidate.

scenarios.draft: Test failure to register seller with missing required fields. Attempt to register a new seller with missing or invalid (e.g., empty) mandatory fields such as company_name, business_number, or password. Validate that the API returns clear validation errors, does not create the account, and that audit logging captures the failed attempt.

Test failure to register seller with an improperly formatted email address (not RFC compliant or not allowed by business rules). Attempt registration and confirm the API returns an error, does not create an account, and records an audit/compliance event.

Test failure to register seller with an already used business number. Register one seller with a unique business_number, then attempt registration of a new seller using the same business_number with a different email. Confirm the API enforces uniqueness, returns a precise error, and audit logs the attempt.

dependencies.purpose: Register the first seller to create a business_number duplication scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test fetching detailed information for a single favorite product using a given favoriteProductId. Cover successful retrieval (for the authenticated customer and if the product is currently favorited), forbidden access (if another user tries to fetch details), and not found scenarios (if the favoriteProductId does not exist or is soft-deleted). Validate the returned fields include favorite and product details. Ensure soft-deleted or non-owned records return an appropriate error indicating either access restriction or missing record.

dependencies.purpose: Obtain a list of currently favorited product IDs for the authenticated customer to use as setup.
Create a favorite product link to ensure a favoriteProductId exists for positive test cases.

scenarios.draft: Test adding a product to the authenticated customer's favorite products list using a valid productId. First, verify successful creation when the product is not already favorited, including validation that the link references the correct customer and product. Test duplicate handling by attempting to favorite the same product twice—ensure the system either returns the existing favorite or an error indicating it's already favorited. Also test invalid productId and validation errors (e.g., non-existent or deleted product).

dependencies.purpose: Check for existing favorites to confirm initial state is correct.

scenarios.draft: Test updating a favorite product entry's metadata and performing a soft-unfavorite (set deleted_at). Cover successful updates to allowed fields by the authenticated owner, disallowing updates by other users. Ensure proper business logic on soft-unfavorite—after unfavoriting, the record should no longer appear in active queries. Attempt updates on non-existent, non-owned, or already soft-deleted records and verify correct error handling/response codes. Confirm side effects such as notification cleanup or analytics adjustment as appropriate.

dependencies.purpose: Create a favorite product record to provide a valid favoriteProductId for update/unfavorite testing.

scenarios.draft: Test soft-deleting (unfavoriting) a favorite product by its ID for the authenticated customer. Cover the normal path (deleting an existing favorite), and error scenarios, including already soft-deleted entries and unauthorized deletion attempts. Confirm that deleted records do not show in active favorite lists but still exist for audit purposes. Test idempotent behavior on repeat deletion calls and ensure associated notifications or recommendation entries are updated upon unfavoriting. Attempt to delete a favoriteProductId that never existed and verify appropriate error is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create a valid favoriteProductId for the test, ensuring the record exists for delete/unfavorite actions.

scenarios.draft: Test searching and paginating through a customer's favorite inquiry records. Cover successful retrieval with default and advanced filter criteria (e.g. by inquiry status, title/content, date ranges) and proper pagination. Validate that only favorites belonging to the authenticated customer are returned, and that soft-deleted (unfavorited) entries and inaccessible records are excluded. Test edge cases of empty result sets, invalid filters, unauthorized access attempts, and out-of-bounds pagination parameters. Ensure auditing and notification requirements are respected as described in the business rules.

dependencies.purpose: Establish at least one favorite inquiry record for the user to enable search/filter testing.

scenarios.draft: Test successful retrieval of a specific order item detail by the owning customer. First, create a new customer and log in to receive an authentication token. Next, create an order for this customer, add an order item, and then fetch the detail of that specific order item using its orderId and orderItemId. Validate that the returned item information matches expected fields and that access is granted. This test simulates a typical user reviewing their order item after purchase.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new customer account to obtain user identity and permission context.
Authenticate as the newly registered customer to obtain a JWT token for authorized API access.
Create a new order for the customer so there is an order context to add items to.
Add a new item to the created order and obtain the orderItemId needed for the GET detail test.

scenarios.draft: Verify that an authenticated customer cannot access the order item detail of another customer's order. Register two distinct customer accounts. Have the first customer place an order and add an order item. Attempt to fetch the order item detail as the second customer using the same orderId and orderItemId, and confirm that the system returns a 'forbidden' error response to enforce ownership access control.

dependencies.purpose: Register both customers needed for this test, ensuring separate identities.
Log into each customer account as part of the test sequence.
Create an order for the first customer to own the test order item.
Add an item to the order, establishing the context for secure ownership.

scenarios.draft: Test handling of requests for a non-existent order item. Register and authenticate a customer, create an order, and attempt to fetch an order item detail using an invalid or random orderItemId that does not exist under the specified orderId. Verify that the system returns an appropriate 'not found' error, validating error handling for invalid references.

dependencies.purpose: Register customer for authentication context.
Authenticate as the customer.
Create an order to provide a legitimate orderId for testing error response to non-existent orderItemId.

scenarios.draft: Verify that an authenticated seller can view the details of an order item associated with their product sale. Register a seller account, create a product, and make a sale via a customer order. The seller then retrieves the order item detail using the correct orderId and orderItemId. The test validates proper business linkage, access permissions, and that the returned data is correct for the seller's product.

dependencies.purpose: Register a seller to manage products and monitor order sales.
Authenticate as the seller for JWT authorization.
Create a product under the seller's ownership to be included in customer orders.
Register a customer to simulate a buyer.
Login as customer to place an order.
Customer creates an order for the seller's product.
Customer adds an order item referencing the seller's product, enabling the seller to later check details.

scenarios.draft: Test that a seller cannot access the details of an order item not related to their own product sales. Register two sellers, ensure a product and order for the first seller, then attempt to fetch the order item detail as the second seller. Validate the system returns a 'forbidden' or similar access-denied response, ensuring robust enforcement of data privacy.

dependencies.purpose: Create both seller accounts to establish separate business entities.
Login as the second seller to attempt unauthorized data access.
Register a product owned by Seller 1 for sale.
Register a customer for test ordering.
Customer login for order placement.
Customer order referencing Seller 1's product.
Customer creates an order item for Seller 1's product.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin user can retrieve details of any order item across the system, regardless of order ownership. Register an admin user, create a customer and order with an order item, then have the admin fetch the order item detail. Verify all fields are viewable and compliance/audit access is logged as per policy.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin user for privileged access.
Authenticate as admin for JWT token.
Register a customer to create an order with items.
Login as customer to initiate order.
Create order for the customer.
Create order item under the customer's order, setup for admin testing.

scenarios.draft: Verify that the system returns an appropriate error when an admin tries to fetch an order item detail using an invalid or non-existent orderItemId. Register an admin, and attempt to fetch with a fake or random ID. The response should be a 'not found' error, confirming correct error handling for invalid identifiers at admin level.

dependencies.purpose: Register admin to perform the test with high privileges.
Authenticate as admin.

scenarios.draft: Test the ability for an authenticated customer to add a new item to one of their orders. Register and login a customer, create a new order, then post a new order item referencing a valid product. Validate the response includes the created item, proper snapshot linkage, and order item constraints are enforced (e.g., quantity, valid product relationship).

dependencies.purpose: Register new customer.
Authenticate for API access.
Create seller for the product catalog.
Seller login to create products.
Seller creates a new product to be ordered.
Customer creates a new order in which the order item will be added.

scenarios.draft: Verify that the system returns an error when attempting to add an order item referencing a productId that does not exist or is not available. Register and login as customer, create a new order, then attempt to add an order item with a random or non-existent productId. Confirm system rejects the creation with a validation or not found error response.

dependencies.purpose: Register customer.
Login as customer for authorized operation.
Create order for context in which to add the item.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to add an order item to an order while unauthenticated (no JWT token provided). Confirm that the system denies the operation, returning an 'unauthorized' or 'authentication required' error. This tests enforcement of access controls on item creation.

dependencies.purpose: Create an order context (if required) to which to attempt the unauthorized add action.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin can directly add a new order item to any customer's order. Register an admin, register a customer and create an order for them, then have the admin add a new order item to this order. Validate the admin's ability to create items across ownership boundaries, and that the created item is associated with the correct order.

dependencies.purpose: Register admin for privileged action.
Login as admin to obtain necessary JWT.
Create a customer to own the target order.
Customer logs in to create the order.
Create the target order for admin's order item insertion.

scenarios.draft: Verify that the admin receives an error when trying to add an order item referencing a non-existent or invalid product. Register admin, create a customer and an order, then attempt to add an order item referencing a fake productId. The response should be a validation error or 'not found' error, validating input constraint enforcement.

dependencies.purpose: Register admin.
Authenticate as admin.
Create customer for the order context.
Customer logs in to create the order.
Create an order to which admin will attempt to attach an invalid order item.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieval of coupon snapshots with advanced filtering and pagination as an admin. Simulate different filter, sort, and pagination parameters (e.g., by couponTemplateId, created_at range, status), ensuring that only admin-role accounts have access and the returned data matches the filters. Edge cases include empty results and large result sets. Also, verify error handling for malformed queries and unauthorized access. Use dependency to authenticate as admin user before the request.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as admin to obtain JWT for authorization.

scenarios.draft: Test fetching a specific coupon snapshot detail by its UUID as admin. Scenario 1: Successful retrieval for an existing, non-deleted snapshot. Scenario 2: Attempt to fetch a non-existent or soft-deleted snapshot, verifying correct not-found/appropriate error is returned. Check that only admin-role accounts can access the detail. Dependency: Authenticate as admin before executing the GET request.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as admin to obtain JWT for authorization.

scenarios.draft: Test creation of a new coupon snapshot as an admin. Scenario 1: Provide valid payload with correct references to an existing coupon and event context, expect successful creation with compliance audit fields. Scenario 2: Attempt to create a snapshot with duplicate (already used) data or invalid reference (e.g., non-existent issued coupon or event), ensuring system returns validation or conflict error. Edge: Missing required field. Dependency: Authenticate as admin and create a valid issued coupon before snapshot creation.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as admin to obtain JWT for authorization.
Issue a valid coupon to be referenced in the snapshot payload.

scenarios.draft: Update allowed fields of a coupon snapshot record as an admin. Scenario: Update metadata or permissible fields (not evidence/immutable data) for an existing, non-deleted snapshot and verify success. Try forbidden mutations (changing immutable fields or for a non-existent/deleted snapshot) and verify validation or error responses. Ensure audit logging occurs as required. Dependency: Create a valid coupon snapshot before updating.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as admin to obtain JWT for authorization.
Create a coupon snapshot that will be targeted for updates.

scenarios.draft: Perform soft-delete of a coupon snapshot by its UUID as admin. Scenario 1: Delete an existing, active coupon snapshot and verify 'deleted_at' is set and record is omitted from active listings, but still retained for audit. Scenario 2: Attempt to delete a non-existent or already-deleted snapshot and verify not-found or idempotency is correctly handled. Confirm only admin role can delete, and that audit/compliance traces are logged. Dependency: Create and optionally delete a coupon snapshot.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as admin to obtain JWT for authorization.
Create a coupon snapshot for testing deletion.

scenarios.draft: Test searching favorite snapshot records as an admin using advanced filtering options. Cover scenarios including search by time window, object type (product, inquiry, address), customer constraints, and keyword queries on snapshot contents. Validate correct pagination, sorting, and access control. Confirm that only authorized admin users can retrieve snapshot details. Verify correct behavior for empty searches, invalid filter parameters, and permission errors. Edge cases should include requests with no matching data and searches at page boundaries.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin user to acquire a valid admin JWT for testing authorized access.
Login as an admin to obtain JWT for authorization when listing favorite snapshots.

scenarios.draft: Test fetching a favorite snapshot record by its unique ID as the owner (customer). Validate that only the owner or authorized admin can access the record. Ensure the response contains historical snapshot content as expected, and that attempts to access non-existent, deleted, or non-owned snapshots yield suitable errors. Edge cases should include requesting with unauthorized users and soft-deleted records.

dependencies.purpose: Register a customer account to serve as the owner of the favorite snapshot.
Login as the customer to obtain JWT for authorized requests.
Favorite a product as the customer, creating a favorite record needed to snapshot.
Create a favorite snapshot for the customer to retrieve by ID.

scenarios.draft: Test fetching a favorite snapshot record by its unique ID as an admin, who is not the owner. Validate proper permission checks and information disclosure consistent with admin roles. Cover attempts to retrieve existing, deleted, and non-existent snapshot records, ensuring correct error codes and audit trail enforcement.

dependencies.purpose: Register a customer to create a favorite and related snapshot.
Allow creation of favorite product and favorite snapshot as a customer.
Create a favorite product as the customer for snapshot creation.
Customer creates a favorite snapshot to be accessed by admin.
Register a new admin for snapshot retrieval.
Login as admin to obtain token for authorized get requests.

scenarios.draft: Test creating a favorite snapshot for a valid, active favorite object (e.g., product, inquiry, or address) as the owner customer. Validate that the snapshot record is correctly created and returned, including all references and serialized object state. Then, attempt to create a duplicate snapshot for the same favorite object and verify that the system properly enforces idempotency or returns an appropriate error, per business logic. Also test creating a snapshot for a favorite object that is not active (e.g., soft-deleted) or not owned by the customer, confirming correct business rule enforcement and error messages.

dependencies.purpose: Register a customer account as the owner of the favorite.
Login as customer to perform authed operations.
Create a favorite object (product) as a prerequisite for snapshot creation.

scenarios.draft: Test updating a favorite snapshot record as the snapshot's owner, modifying permitted metadata or object state. Validate that only allowed fields are updateable—attempts to change immutable or restricted fields (such as creation timestamp) must be rejected. Test error handling for updating non-existent, deleted, or non-owned favoriteSnapshotId records. Confirm successful updates are reflected in the returned entity, and non-permitted fields remain unchanged. Ensure security checks for role and ownership are strictly enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Register and login as a customer to act as snapshot owner.
Obtain authentication for performing snapshot creation and update.
Create a favorite product as a base for the snapshot.
Create an initial favorite snapshot as the customer, for update testing.

scenarios.draft: Test updating mutable metadata for an existing product review snapshot by an admin. First, create a customer and log in, then have the customer create a product, place an order, and write a product review. Have the customer (or admin) create a snapshot of the review. Finally, as an admin, update the metadata for a review snapshot (such as compliance annotations or context) and verify the update is reflected, previous audit trail is preserved, and no illegal fields (core review content, timestamps) can be changed. Verify success and audit integrity.

dependencies.purpose: Create and authenticate an admin user to perform the update.
Create a customer account for review creation.
Authenticate the customer for subsequent operations.
Create a product review to ensure a valid review context for snapshot creation.
Create a review snapshot for the product review to allow later update.

scenarios.draft: Test update failure when trying to modify immutable fields (e.g., core review content, rating, created_at) of an existing review snapshot by an admin. Attempt to change a protected field and verify that the API rejects the request, returns a descriptive error, does not alter snapshot data or audit trail, and enforces compliance policies.

dependencies.purpose: Create and authenticate an admin user account.
Create a customer for the review creation.
Authenticate as the customer.
Create a product review to establish review context.
Create a review snapshot to be updated.

scenarios.draft: Test soft deletion (erase) of a product review snapshot by an admin. Create a customer and their product review, have the admin create a snapshot for the review, then, as admin, delete the snapshot (soft delete). Verify that the snapshot is excluded from standard queries, audit log records the action, and other snapshots remain accessible. Confirm that deletion is not permitted if the snapshot is under a compliance lock or legal hold.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin account and log in.
Register a customer to create product reviews.
Authenticate as customer.
Create a product review for snapshotting.
Create a review snapshot for testing deletion.

scenarios.draft: Test idempotency and error handling for repeated or invalid review snapshot soft deletion. After deleting a review snapshot, attempt to delete it again and confirm the API returns an appropriate error or idempotent success. Also, attempt to delete a non-existent snapshot and validate the error response is precise and audit-tracked.

dependencies.purpose: Prepare an admin user for erase action.
Create a customer for context.
Customer login for review creation.
Produce a review and snapshot to delete.
Create the target review snapshot.

scenarios.draft: Test advanced search and filtering of moderation events by an admin. Insert multiple moderation events (covering different event types, actors, review/inquiry targets, and date ranges) and query them with different filter criteria (by event type, actor_type, date, or specific target entities). Validate that only the correct, authorized, and relevant moderation events are returned, responses are paginated, and sensitive data is filtered or exposed as per admin role. Edge cases: search with empty filter returns all (up to page limit), filters for non-existent criteria return empty result, and pagination works correctly.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin account for advanced search access.
Insert moderation event records with diverse values for search testing.

scenarios.draft: Test search request as a non-admin (e.g., customer or seller) and confirm the API returns an authorization error and logs the access attempt for compliance. Create a non-admin user, authenticate, then attempt to search moderation events as this user.

dependencies.purpose: Register a customer for unauthorized access.
Authenticate as the customer.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieval of moderation event detail by UUID as an admin. First, create an admin, then insert a moderation event. Call the GET endpoint with the correct moderationEventId and validate the complete event data (event type, actor, target entities, reasons, evidence, timestamp) is accurate, sensitive fields are included, and audit logs record the access.

dependencies.purpose: Create and login as an admin to get moderation event details.
Insert a moderation event to query by ID.

scenarios.draft: Test error handling when retrieving a moderationEventId that does not exist or has been deleted. As an admin, attempt to fetch a detail with a random or erased UUID, verify a not-found error is returned, and confirm audit logs are updated for compliance and incident traceability.

dependencies.purpose: Admin context for the GET request.

scenarios.draft: Test creation of a new moderation event by an admin for a review or inquiry. Steps: prepare a resource (e.g., a product review or inquiry), have an admin trigger a POST with event details such as type, actor, target entity, evidence references, and reason. Validate that the moderation event is persisted, all business-required fields are present, the target status is updated accordingly (e.g., review blocked/unblocked), and the event is recorded in audit/compliance logs. Subsequent GET/listing should include this moderation event.

dependencies.purpose: Admin account creation to perform moderation action.
Create a product review to moderate (alternatively, use a product inquiry as target).

scenarios.draft: Test failure case for creation of moderation event with invalid parameters (e.g., missing required field, referencing non-existent review/inquiry, or providing illegal event_type). Ensure API validation triggers, returns explicit error messages, does not create the moderation event, and audits the failed attempt for compliance.

dependencies.purpose: Admin user for context.

scenarios.draft: Test successful retrieval of a paginated and filtered list of order groups as an admin. Provide various search criteria, such as group name, external reference, and date ranges. Ensure that the response returns a correctly filtered, sorted, and paginated set of results. Validate that only users with admin role can access full results, and that empty searches result in empty datasets with valid pagination. Attempt with both matching and non-matching filters to cover happy path and no-result scenarios.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an admin to receive a valid JWT token required to authorize the order group search.
Create at least one order group as test data before attempting to search and filter.

scenarios.draft: Test that a non-admin user (customer or seller) is denied access when attempting to search admin order groups. Attempt the API with an invalid or missing JWT token, expecting a forbidden error or invalid authentication response. Validate security and RBAC configuration.

Test failure when the admin tries to search for order groups using invalid search or filter parameters (e.g., invalid sort parameter, malformed filter conditions). The system should return a meaningful error (e.g., validation failed) and compliance-appropriate error code. Confirm no data is leaked and the error structure is useful for troubleshooting.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as admin for permission to access the endpoint.

scenarios.draft: Test successful retrieval of an order group by its ID for a customer who is authorized to view the group. Ensure all relevant order group details (metadata, notes, and batch references) are included. Also test that another customer who does not own the group cannot access the order group, and receives an appropriate permission denied error. Cover edge cases such as invalid UUID format and group not found.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new customer to simulate a user-facing scenario.
Obtain a JWT token for customer who owns the order group.
Create an order group and assign it to the test customer.

scenarios.draft: Test successful detailed retrieval of an order group by group ID for an authorized seller. Validate that all business metadata is accurate and complete. Attempt to retrieve a group with a seller who does not have ownership or permission and confirm a forbidden or not-found error is returned. Also test error cases for missing or malformed orderGroupId parameter.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new seller to simulate selling context.
Obtain JWT for seller to use the API.
Admin creates an order group linked to seller's business for testing access and ownership.

scenarios.draft: Validate admin can successfully retrieve complete details for an order group by its ID, seeing all admin-only fields. Cover edge cases such as requesting with a nonexistent orderGroupId (should return not found), attempting with an invalid UUID format, or with insufficient permissions/non-admin context (should return forbidden or error). Confirm audit is triggered for such access.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as admin for permission.
Admin creates an order group (setup for the fetch scenario).

scenarios.draft: Verify admin is able to successfully create a new order group by supplying all required fields. Validate system response structure and side effects such as audit event creation. Additionally, attempt to create another order group with identical unique attributes (if any exist in the schema—e.g., group name for the same time period) to check system behavior for duplicate prevention or proper error response. Also test failures for missing, malformed, or unauthorized parameters.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as admin to enable order group creation.

scenarios.draft: Test successful retrieval of a specific access log entry by a valid admin user. Precondition: Ensure an admin user is authenticated and an access log entry exists. The admin requests the log by its accessLogId. Verify that the full log detail is returned, including timestamp, actor identity, source IP, and action context. Confirm that returned data matches the record in the underlying audit table, and no sensitive data is disclosed beyond permitted scope.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate admin and obtain JWT for authorization.
Search and retrieve a list of existing access logs to extract a valid accessLogId for detail retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieval of an access log entry that does not exist or was already deleted. The admin requests a non-existent accessLogId. Verify the API returns an appropriate not found error and does not disclose any sensitive information. Ensure error response contains a proper error code and message for audit/compliance.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate admin and obtain JWT for authorization.

scenarios.draft: Test unauthorized access to a specific access log. Attempt the request as a non-admin user (e.g., as a customer or seller), or with no token, or with a revoked JWT. Verify the endpoint returns a permission denied error and logs the access attempt for compliance. Ensure no access log details are leaked.

dependencies.purpose: Register a customer to acquire a non-admin JWT for negative test.

scenarios.draft: Test the ability of an authenticated admin to search and retrieve a paginated, filtered list of security logs. Filter by event type (e.g., failed_login), actor type, severity, or time window. Confirm the API returns a correctly paged and filtered result set that matches search criteria with no errors. Results should not include unauthorized information.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate admin and obtain JWT for search.
Setup/test for existing log records to validate presence of filterable log entries.

scenarios.draft: Test permission enforcement by attempting to search security logs with a non-admin role (e.g., customer or seller). Request must fail with a 403 or similar error, and no log data should be returned.

dependencies.purpose: Register a seller and use their credentials to attempt log search.

scenarios.draft: Test that invalid search/filter criteria (e.g., malformed filter values or invalid enum values) result in an explicit error response without a server crash. Validate that the error is properly structured and audit/compliance fields are unaffected.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as admin for search.

scenarios.draft: Test successful retrieval of a security log entry by valid securityLogId as an admin. Confirm that the returned record matches the schema, includes all required audit fields, and does not leak unrelated data. Cross-verify with log search results.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate admin to get JWT.
Search security logs to obtain a valid securityLogId for detail request.

scenarios.draft: Request a securityLogId that does not exist or is deleted. Ensure system returns a standardized not found error without disclosing implementation details. Error should be logged.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as admin.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to retrieve a security log entry as a non-admin user (customer or seller) or without authentication. Validate that a permission denied error and proper audit log is returned, and no log details are leaked.

dependencies.purpose: Register a customer to obtain a non-admin JWT for negative permission testing.

scenarios.draft: Test successful search and retrieval of system events with specific filters such as event_type, time range, or severity. As an admin, execute a search and validate that only matching, paginated event summaries are returned. Confirm that system event fields are complete and no over-fetch occurs.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as admin for system event search.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to search system events with an unauthorized or non-admin user. Ensure the API correctly rejects the request and returns no event data.

dependencies.purpose: Register a seller for unauthorized role testing.

scenarios.draft: Provide invalid or malformed search criteria (e.g., wrong enum value, invalid date) to system events search. Expect the API to respond with a clear, schema-compliant error without crashing or leaking system data.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as admin for negative test scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieval by admin of a valid system event record. Confirm that the API retrieves and returns full event information, including event type, summary, payload, severity, and timestamps. Ensure record matches previously listed record from search endpoint and no sensitive system data is exposed.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate admin and obtain JWT for event retrieval.
System event search to obtain a valid systemEventId.

scenarios.draft: Request a system event record by an invalid or previously deleted systemEventId as admin. The API should return a clean not found error without side effects or exposing underlying implementation details. Confirm that the error response matches contract.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate for negative test case.

scenarios.draft: Request a system event record as a non-admin user or unauthenticated. API should strictly enforce admin-only access and return a permission denied error, with no disclosure of event content or metadata.

dependencies.purpose: Register a seller for negative test case.

scenarios.draft: Test the successful retrieval of a favorite address detail by the owning customer. The customer creates a new address, marks it as favorite, and retrieves it via the detail endpoint. The test validates that all address metadata, timestamps, and personalization context fields are accurate and accessible only by the owner. Ensure correct data returned for active favorite addresses. Confirm response structure matches schema.

dependencies.purpose: Create a favorite address as the current customer to obtain a valid favoriteAddressId for detail retrieval. Address creation is prerequisite for access test.

scenarios.draft: Test that a customer cannot retrieve the detail of a favorite address belonging to a different customer. One user creates a favorite address, and another user attempts access by ID. Confirm that the API returns an access denied or not found error and does not expose address data of other customers. This is critical for privacy enforcement.

dependencies.purpose: Register the owner customer who will create the favorite address.
Create favorite address under the owner customer before testing unauthorized access by a second user.

scenarios.draft: Test response when requesting the detail for a non-existent favoriteAddressId. Attempt to retrieve details for a favoriteAddressId that does not exist or has been soft-deleted, and verify the API returns a proper not found error without exposing data. Ensure error format matches API standard.

Test deleting a shopping cart snapshot as the authorized customer. First, create an authenticated customer and ensure the customer has a valid shopping cart. Add items to the cart and create at least one cart snapshot. Attempt to delete the snapshot by ID. Verify that the snapshot is logically removed (soft delete), and subsequent retrieval is disallowed. Also test error conditions: deleting a non-existent snapshot, non-owned snapshot, or an already-deleted snapshot should result in appropriate error responses.

dependencies.purpose: Register and login a customer to perform cart-related actions.
Create a new cart for the customer.
Create a cart snapshot to be used for the deletion scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a paginated and filtered list of payment records for an order as the valid customer. First, create and authenticate a customer, and create an order. Add one or more payments to the order, then search orderPayments with filters such as payment method or date range, and verify correct pagination and filtering. Also, attempt to search payments for an order that belongs to another customer (permission error), and search for an order that does not exist (not found).

dependencies.purpose: Register and login a customer to perform order payment searches.
Create a new order for the customer.
Add payment(s) to the order for test data setup.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving and filtering order payment records as an admin for compliance and audit use. First, login as an admin user. Create an order (using customer or admin flows), add multiple payment records to the order, and perform searches with varied filter criteria (e.g., date ranges, payment method, transaction status). Validate that results reflect all matching payments, compliance pagination is accurate, and sensitive data appears as permitted by role. Attempt to query an order that does not exist (should return not found) and verify that unauthorized users cannot access the endpoint.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an admin with the correct permissions.
Create an order to be managed by admin for test coverage.
Create payment(s) to associate with the order.

scenarios.draft: Test fetching details for a specific order payment as the correct customer. Register a customer, create an order, and attach a payment. Retrieve the payment by its ID and verify all fields are correct. Attempt to fetch a payment for a non-owned order or a non-existent payment, confirming that access is denied or not found is returned as appropriate. This tests both happy path and strict access control on payment data.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate and setup the customer context.
Create an order to associate a payment with.
Create a payment record attached to the order.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a specific order payment record as an admin. Log in as admin, ensure an order exists with at least one payment. Fetch the payment by its ID as admin and verify complete data (including audit fields). Attempt to access a payment using a nonexistent payment ID (should return not found). Also, attempt access with insufficient privileges or for an order that does not exist to ensure correct error handling and logging for audit.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an admin.
Create a customer order for associating with payments.
Create payment(s) as test fixtures to check detail retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Verify an admin can successfully search and paginate cart items within a specified cart. Start by creating a customer and registering an admin, then have the customer create a cart and add multiple items, each with varying product IDs, quantities, and statuses. As the admin, search for cart items in that cart using assorted filters such as product ID, status, creation date, and with pagination (e.g., page 1, page 2). Validate that the correct items are returned based on the filter criteria, pagination metadata is accurate, and that any business rules for search and filter are enforced. The admin should see all items, including those created by the customer.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new customer to own the cart.
Register an admin to perform the search action.
Customer creates a cart to add items into.
Add several cart items to enable search and filter scenarios.

scenarios.draft: Test that a non-owning customer is unable to search/paginate cart items in another customer's cart via the admin endpoint. Register two customers (A and B). Customer A creates a cart and cart items. Customer B, without admin rights, attempts to access the admin search endpoint for A's cart items and should receive a forbidden or permission denied error as per business logic.

dependencies.purpose: Register both customer A and customer B.
Customer A creates a cart.
Add items to Customer A's cart to test unauthorized access by B.

scenarios.draft: Verify a customer can retrieve full details of a cart item from their own cart. First, register a customer and create a cart. Add an item to the cart. Fetch the added cart item's details by providing both cartId and cartItemId and assert that all metadata including product info, optionId, quantity, and timestamps are accurate and correspond to the item added.

dependencies.purpose: Register customer for cart ownership.
Customer creates a cart.
Add a cart item.

scenarios.draft: Validate that accessing a nonexistent cart item returns an appropriate not found error. Register a customer and create a cart. Attempt to fetch a cart item detail using a random or invalid cartItemId within the valid cart, and verify that a clear error message or not found response is returned, and no sensitive cart data is leaked.

dependencies.purpose: Register a customer to own a cart.
Customer creates a cart.

scenarios.draft: Check that an admin can retrieve details of any customer's cart item, regardless of ownership. Register a customer and create a cart, then add a cart item as the customer. As an admin, fetch the item's detail via the admin endpoint using both cartId and cartItemId, verifying all data is returned, and compliance audit fields are populated. Confirm the admin can access details even if the cart owner differs.

dependencies.purpose: Register customer who owns the cart.
Register admin for privileged access.
Customer creates the cart.
Customer adds a cart item.

scenarios.draft: Ensure the admin receives a not found error if attempting to fetch a cart item with an invalid cartItemId or cartId. After registering an admin, attempt to fetch details of a nonexistent (random UUID) cartItemId or cartId and confirm that the system responds with a clear not found error, without leaking details about whether the cart exists or about other users.

dependencies.purpose: Register admin for access to the GET endpoint.

scenarios.draft: Test successful addition of a new unique cart item to a customer's cart. Register a customer and create a cart. Add a cart item with a unique productId and quantity. Assert the returned cart item matches the inputs and that the cart's item count increases appropriately. Confirm business validation for optional fields such as optionId and unit price, as per schema.

dependencies.purpose: Register the customer for cart creation.
Customer creates a cart.

scenarios.draft: Check system validation when attempting to add a duplicate cart item (same productId and optionId if applicable) into the same cart. Register a customer, create a cart, and add a cart item. Attempt to add the exact same item again. The system should reject the duplicate and return an appropriate error message, enforcing uniqueness constraint within the cart.

dependencies.purpose: Register customer for the workflow.
Create cart for the customer.
Add the initial cart item for duplicate test.

scenarios.draft: Admin should be able to create a cart item on behalf of any customer. Register both an admin and a customer, then create a cart for the customer. As the admin, use the admin endpoint to add a new cart item to the customer's cart, specifying a product and quantity. Validate the item is added successfully and the cart's integrity is preserved, confirming business and security logic allow admin-mediated item addition.

dependencies.purpose: Register the admin privileged user.
Register the customer who owns the cart.
Customer creates the cart before admin operation.

scenarios.draft: Test admin-side error handling when referencing a nonexistent cartId or productId while attempting to add a cart item. Register an admin and attempt to add a cart item to a random or invalid cartId, or with a bad productId. The API should return a not found or validation error without altering system state. Confirm the error message is explicit, and no extraneous information is revealed.

dependencies.purpose: Register the admin for test execution.

scenarios.draft: Simulate an admin updating product content for an existing product with valid, business-compliant attributes. The scenario begins with an admin creating a product and associated product content. Then, the content fields such as content_type, content_uri, display_order, or description are updated with appropriate values. Assert that the update operation succeeds, the returned record matches the new input values, and that audit fields (updated_at, updated_by) are properly refreshed.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new product as an admin for associating content.
Register an initial product content record to be targeted for update. Must use returned productId and productContentId for the update test.

scenarios.draft: Simulate an admin attempting to update product content with changes to forbidden or immutable fields, such as product_id, contentId, or illegal changes to core system-generated fields. The system must reject the update, producing clear error responses and maintaining integrity of immutable data. Include audit trail validation for failed update.

dependencies.purpose: Create product for setup.
Create product content to be used in the update failure scenario.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to update a product content record that does not exist (using an invalid or random UUID for productContentId). The system should return a not found error and leave the product state unchanged. Business logic must indicate that update cannot operate on missing records, even if the parent product exists.

dependencies.purpose: Create product for use in preparing the test. No corresponding content record is created; the contentId supplied to the test is intentionally invalid.

scenarios.draft: Perform a paginated search for seller-relevant orders using advanced filter criteria (by status, customer info, total amount, and date range). The test will ensure that filtering, sorting, and pagination return the correct subset of orders, with accurate result counts, links, and summary fields. Business validation should confirm that only orders associated with the seller role are visible and access is denied for orders outside their remit.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new seller account for authentication.
Authenticate as seller and obtain token for use in requests.
A customer creates orders containing products linked to the seller.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to search seller orders with insufficient permissions, such as using a customer or admin user's credentials, or no credentials at all. The response should be a permission error, and no order data must leak.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin account.
Authenticate as admin and attempt to use seller order search endpoint.

scenarios.draft: Search for seller orders using extreme filters that guarantee no results (such as an unrealistically high order total, or future-only date range). Verify that the API returns a valid, empty result set, with correct paging information and no error status.

dependencies.purpose: Register seller and obtain authentication for an account with no associated orders.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to search seller orders using invalid or malformed filter criteria, such as a non-numeric value for an amount range or an invalid date string. The API should return a validation error, and must not process or return any records.

dependencies.purpose: Setup seller account for authentication.

scenarios.draft: Test advanced order search as an admin, using multiple filter parameters such as customer, status, total amount, order group, and custom date ranges. Validate that pagination, sorting, and advanced query result structure match business requirements. Confirm that all orders, regardless of seller or customer, are accessible, and that admin can see detailed audit fields. Edge case with multi-page result should be tested.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin account.
Authenticate as admin.
Customer creates several orders to ensure multiple pages of results exist.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to perform admin order search using a seller or customer user's credentials, or without authentication. Validate that access is denied and no order data is disclosed.

dependencies.purpose: Register customer for negative permission testing.
Login as customer and attempt admin order search.

scenarios.draft: As admin, search order records using rare filter combinations (non-existent customer, impossible total amount, etc.) that guarantee no orders are found. Confirm that an empty result set is returned with the appropriate pagination structure and no error is raised.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin for search operations.
Admin login prior to performing search.

scenarios.draft: Simulate a seller deleting a product content from their own product. Begin by authenticating as a seller, creating a product, and adding product content. Then, attempt to delete the product content and confirm that the resource is removed from UI and APIs but is preserved for compliance or rollback. Validate that subsequent attempts to get the deleted content produce a not found error or show soft-deleted status depending on system design.

dependencies.purpose: Register a seller account for own-product test.
Login as the seller.
Seller creates a product.
Create product content as the seller for target of deletion.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to delete a product content belonging to another seller. The operation should fail with a permission error, and the content must remain present. Set up at least two sellers and ensure that only the content owner can delete their content.

dependencies.purpose: Register two seller accounts for cross-ownership test.
Login as seller B (not the owner of the product content).
Seller A creates a product and product content.
Seller A adds product content to be tested for cross-owner deletion.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to delete a product content record that does not exist using a random or invalid productContentId. The endpoint should return a not found error and leave all product content unchanged. Confirm that deletion is idempotent and does not affect system state.

dependencies.purpose: Register seller account.

dependencies.purpose: Register a customer who will own the inquiry.

Explicitly create a snapshot for targeted retrieval.

Confirm detailed response matches expected point-in-time data, and access is allowed only for inquiries tied to the seller's products. dependencies.purpose: Prepare a seller for product/inquiry ownership.

Generate an inquiry for the product.
Generate a snapshot for the inquiry.

Soft-delete a snapshot for negative test on retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Test successful update of an existing order payment by the customer who owns the order. dependencies.purpose: Register a new customer.
Create an order for the customer.

scenarios.draft: Test update failure when attempting to update a non-existent order payment. Try updating an orderPaymentId that does not exist for a real order and verify a not found or validation error is returned according to API and no data is modified.

Create an order for the customer.

scenarios.draft: Test successful update of an order payment by an admin user. The admin updates allowed fields of a payment initially created by a customer or admin for a certain order. dependencies.purpose: Register an admin for update action.

Create a new order.
Admin creates an initial payment to later update.

scenarios.draft: Test that admin is not able to update immutable, restricted, or non-existent payment records. Attempt to update an orderPaymentId that either does not exist or references disallowed fields, and verify the API returns the correct permission or not found error, and no update occurs.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin user.
Register a customer and create an order.
Customer order for context.

scenarios.draft: Test that an authenticated customer can successfully (soft/hard) delete a payment record from their own order, according to business rules and schema. Related audit trails and data consistency must be verified.

Place a new order as a customer.
Create an order payment to later delete.

scenarios.draft: Test failure when trying to delete a payment record that does not exist for the customer's order (e.g., bad payment ID or already deleted). Attempt the operation and verify a not found or idempotent success/error is returned, and no side effects occur.

dependencies.purpose: Customer registration for context.
Create an order to use when attempting payment deletion.

scenarios.draft: Test successful update of a product inquiry by an admin. scenarios.draft: Test update attempt by an unauthorized or unauthenticated user. Use a valid productInquiryId, but omit admin authentication or simulate insufficient privileges. The API should return a permission error, preventing the update operation. Dependency: create an inquiry under a customer session; then attempt update under an unauthorized context.

dependencies.purpose: Create a product inquiry for update attempt.

scenarios.draft: Test successful soft-deletion of a product inquiry by its owner customer. The customer authenticates, creates an inquiry, and then deletes it using the provided inquiryId. API should set deleted_at, exclude record from future queries, and return success (no content).

dependencies.purpose: Create a product inquiry that can be deleted by the test customer.

scenarios.draft: Test attempt to delete a non-existent or already-deleted inquiry as a customer. The API should return an error indicating that the record was not found or already deleted. Use inquiry creation and deletion as dependencies, then attempt to delete again.

dependencies.purpose: Create a product inquiry for control.
First delete the inquiry, then re-attempt deletion to test not found scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test attempt to delete a product inquiry as a different, non-owner customer. The API should enforce ownership or privilege checks and respond with a permission error. Dependency: create an inquiry with one customer, then attempt deletion as a different authenticated customer.

scenarios.draft: Test successful soft-deletion of a product inquiry by the related seller for their product. Authenticate as a seller who owns the product referenced in the inquiry. dependencies.purpose: Create a product owned by the seller.
